articles.title: Qlik Replicate Log Stream task error: End of time-line reached and all records were applied, task will stop
articles.description: When a reload target is performed on the logstream staging task (parent) you will get the following error in every Log Stream remote task (child) : [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]W: End of timeline, no more records to read (ar_cdc_channel.c:1210) [SORTER ]E: End of…
articles.text: When a reload target is performed on the logstream staging task (parent) you will get the following error in every Log Stream remote task (child) : [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]W: End of timeline, no more records to read (ar_cdc_channel.c:1210) [SORTER ]E: End of time-line reached and all records were applied, task will stop [1020101] (sorter_transaction.c:3486) The task stops replication to the remote task. Environment Qlik Replicate with Log Steam tasks Resolution There are 2 optional ways to resolve this issue: Option 1 : Reload the Log Stream remote (child) task Option 2 : Start the Log Stream stagging task (parent) from the timestamp before its reload. To do this please follow the steoos below: Find the log of the log stream staging task(parent) just before the reload was performed. i.e. reptask_TASKNAMEof_STAGING_TASK?????.lo g. that has a date just before the reload was performed. Go to the end of the log in step one and get the line that says Final saved task state . At the end of the line get the timestamp Once you get the timestamp, you will need to convert the EPOCH time to Server Time Use that time to start the task.

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Log Stream task fails: Error reading audit batch, Timeout while waiting to get data
articles.description: A Qlik Replicate Log Stream task fails with the error: Stream component 'st_0_T03ERP_TGT_QLK_LSS' terminated Cannot initialize subtask Failed while preparing stream component 'st_0_T03ERP_TGT_QLK_LSS'.
articles.text: A Qlik Replicate Log Stream task fails with the error: Stream component 'st_0_T03ERP_TGT_QLK_LSS' terminated Cannot initialize subtask Failed while preparing stream component 'st_0_T03ERP_TGT_QLK_LSS'. Error reading audit batch Timeout while waiting to get data from audit file Resolution Verify that sufficient disk space is available. Clear up space or increase the available quota, then: Remove the Log Stream directory defined on the Log Stream Target This will remove all current files. A backup to a different location is optional. Start the task from timestamp as far back as the retention period on the Source Transactions logs. This will create a new LogStream directory and new sub-directory audit_files. Cause A corrupted metastore.sqllite file. The file is created in the Log Stream target location (LogStream/audit_services directory) when a task is started. Most commonly disk space issues cause the file's corruption. Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Log Stream Task reading from DB2i Source: Error parsing [1020109]
articles.description: A Qlik Replicate log stream task pointing to an iSeries Source Endpoint with more than 300 tables to the task fails. The error logged is: E rror parsing [1020109] Resolution An internal parameter can be configured in the iSeries Source Endpoint, which defines…
articles.text: A Qlik Replicate log stream task pointing to an iSeries Source Endpoint with more than 300 tables to the task fails. The error logged is: E rror parsing [1020109] Resolution An internal parameter can be configured in the iSeries Source Endpoint, which defines the numbers of tables that can be defined. The parameter name is MaxTablesInJournalFilter . To set: Go to the Endpoint connection Switch to the Advanced tab Click Internal Parameters Add MaxTablesInJournalFilter as the parameter Increase the value (default 300 ) to the required number. Related Content Using IBM DB2 for iSeries as a source

articles.title: Qlik Replicate logs W: The access to Oracle view v$containers is not permitted - Missing inserts
articles.description: Qlik Replicate logs the following warning: W: The access to Oracle view v$containers is not permitted The warning occurs when permission to v$containers is not provided. This permission is required for Oracle multi-tenant databases using Pluggable Databases.
articles.text: Qlik Replicate logs the following warning: W: The access to Oracle view v$containers is not permitted The warning occurs when permission to v$containers is not provided. This permission is required for Oracle multi-tenant databases using Pluggable Databases. The task will run even if permission has not been granted. This leads to data loss. Resolution Grant permission to v$containers for the Oracle user executing the task. Command used: GRANT SELECT ON V$CONTAINERS TO ORACLE_USER Cause Redo logs are based on Container IDs and some transaction belongs to the root container. Transaction IDs that contain information with root container ids will not be captured if there isn't any access to V$container . Environment Qlik Replicate Oracle as a source endpoint Internal Investigation ID(s) Case 00070054 CC-8420

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Logstream parent task import fails with SYS-E-HTTPFAIL, SYS-E-HTTPFAIL, Put full task failed.
articles.description: After exporting a Logstream parent task and changing its name, the import fails with: SYS-E-HTTPFAIL, SYS-E-HTTPFAIL, Put full task failed.
articles.text: After exporting a Logstream parent task and changing its name, the import fails with: SYS-E-HTTPFAIL, SYS-E-HTTPFAIL, Put full task failed. Task name: <task_name> Resolution Delete the original Logstream parent task Import the renamed Logstream task Alternatively, if you need two parent tasks: Edit the task JSON based on this example, replacing the task's name with a new one (such as logstreamnewname as seen in our example): Line 8: "target_names": ["logstreamnewname"], Line 41: "target_name": "logstreamnewname", *notes this is the target: Line 43: "database_name": "logstreamnewname" *notes this is the target endpoint: Line 126: "name": "logstreamnewname", *notes this is the target endpoint: Line 132: "path": "C:\\logstreamnewname",​ Import the task Change the target endpoint if needed Cause The Parent Logstream task has wrongfully signalled a duplication of the target. Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate LOGSTREAM Timeout while waiting to get data from audit file
articles.description: In some cases when Replicate can't read from the Staging Folder of a LogStream task for whatever reason (corrupted folder, lack of disk space etc), there could be difficulties to resume the LogStream task after the initial issue is solved.
articles.text: In some cases when Replicate can't read from the Staging Folder of a LogStream task for whatever reason (corrupted folder, lack of disk space etc), there could be difficulties to resume the LogStream task after the initial issue is solved. You might see errors like the below when trying to resume from timestamp: [UTILITIES ]E: Failed to write to audit file <audit_folder directory> [UTILITIES ]E: Timeout while waiting to get data from audit file [1002521] (at_audit_file.c:637) [UTILITIES ]E: Error reading audit batch [1002509] (at_audit_file.c:679) Environment Qlik Replicate 2021.11 (not exclusive) Linux RHEL / Windows Resolution Stop all LogStream and Replication tasks Kill the replicate sessions and process as the audit file is being locked by the process Rename the audit folder of the problematic audit file (the folder is the one described under the endpoint settings: "Staging Folder" in the Replicate UI) Resume LogStream task from timestamp (a few hours before the initial error), then resume replication tasks from the same timestamp If not solved, a reload of the task will be needed Cause Usually, the Replicate process (repctl) is locking the audit file that was being written/read while the issue occurred.

articles.title: Qlik Replicate missing carriage returns in Snowflake
articles.description: Qlik Replicate is missing carriage returns in Snowflake Resolution To keep the Carriage Return (CR), please add the following internal parameter on your Snowflake endpoint: replaceChars The default value is 0x0D,0x which means that CR ( 0x0D) is replaced by…
articles.text: Qlik Replicate is missing carriage returns in Snowflake Resolution To keep the Carriage Return (CR), please add the following internal parameter on your Snowflake endpoint: replaceChars The default value is 0x0D,0x which means that CR ( 0x0D) is replaced by 0x(nothing) To keep all CR, delete the default value. Then Save. Cause This is by design in Replicate because Snowflake targets are loaded with a CSV file where rows are delimited by carriage returns and embedded carriage returns can cause loading issues. Environment Qlik Replicate Snowflake Endpoint

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Moving the Data Directory on the same server to a larger drive
articles.description: The information in this article is provided as-is and to be used at own discretion. Depending on tool(s) used, customization(s), and/or other factors ongoing support on the solution below may not be provided by Qlik Support.
articles.text: The information in this article is provided as-is and to be used at own discretion. Depending on tool(s) used, customization(s), and/or other factors ongoing support on the solution below may not be provided by Qlik Support. Moving the data folder to a larger drive running out of disk space. The default install directory is usually located on the C: drive and as the replicate environment grows larger and the task multiply users will often run out of disk space. To fix this you will need to delete files and free up space. You can also set up notifications on Disk Space. Once that is done the next best thing to do is to move the data folder to a larger drive on the same server. Resolution Change the location in the Windows Registry You can change the location without reinstalling. It requires the modification of the Windows Registry. This allows you to move the data folder and resume the tasks with no data loss and no need to reload the tasks. For instructions, see Changing the Data Directory location on Windows | Qlik Replicate Help . Reinstall If you do not want to make changes to the registry, you can achieve the same by reinstalling Qlik Replicate. This allows you to move the data folder and resume the tasks with no data loss and no need to reload the tasks. Uninstall Qlik Replicate Move the data folder to new location with more storage space available Reinstall Qlik Replicate and point to the new data folder location. Resume the tasks. Related Content How to Move the Data Directory to a Different Replicate Server How to prevent Qlik Replicate services to go down when the disk space utilization is high Environment Qlik Replicate Data Directory

articles.title: Qlik Replicate not able to process ACDOCA SAP HANA Table
articles.description: This Table in SAP HANA is defined at the DB Level with no Primary Key column which using this Endpoint requires the Tables to have a PK on the Table. [SOURCE_UNLOAD ]W: The table 'SAPHANADB'.'ACDOCA' has no PK.
articles.text: This Table in SAP HANA is defined at the DB Level with no Primary Key column which using this Endpoint requires the Tables to have a PK on the Table. [SOURCE_UNLOAD ]W: The table 'SAPHANADB'.'ACDOCA' has no PK. CDC will not work for this table (saphana_endpoint_artifacts.c:872) Resolution If the SAP HANA DB is running in SLT Mode and the access to the Application Layer Tables in the SAP HANA Source you can add the Table to the Qlik Replicate Task and should show the PK's on the table in the Transform Panel under the Table Specifications. Can run the below command to verify if you have access to the Application Layer Table in SAP HANA: select * from SAPHANADB.DD03L where tabname='ACDOCA' The result set from the query against the SAP HANA Source Endpoint will return the Columns and the 6 Column PK that make up this Table PK List. If you do not get the result set the Qlik Replicate user may not have the proper permissions to read this Table. Qlik Replicate Table Transform should show the PK listed for this Table if its setup and user has proper permissions Since the PK's are now showing the current Triggers for the Table will need to be dropped manually and a Reload for the Table so it can recreate the Triggers with the 6 Primary Key columns. Cause The SAP HANA Endpoint was enhanced in the 2022.5 version with the Service Pack 05 applied to read the Metadata information from the SAP HANA Application layer and not from the SAP HANA DB where the PK information would not be found for this Table. The new versions allow the change to query the Application Table DD03L to get the PK details for the Table. Related Content Qlik Replicate November 2022 | What's New? Environment #Qlik Replicate 2022.5 SP05 #Qlik Replicate 2023.5

articles.title: Qlik Replicate November 2023 and FIPS: Release not yet FIPS compliant
articles.description: The upcoming Qlik Replicate November 2023 release has not yet been certified as FIPS-compliant. Customers who require a FIPS-compliant Qlik Replicate version are advised to remain on or upgrade to Qlik Replicate November 2022 or May 2023.
articles.text: The upcoming Qlik Replicate November 2023 release has not yet been certified as FIPS-compliant. Customers who require a FIPS-compliant Qlik Replicate version are advised to remain on or upgrade to Qlik Replicate November 2022 or May 2023. Qlik is actively working towards supporting FIPS compliance in November 2023 and will provide an update once compliance is met and it is appropriate to upgrade. What is FIPS? FIPS (Federal Information Processing Standards) is a set of standards developed by the United States Federal Government for use in computer systems. FIPS 140-2 is the subset of standards that defines approved encryption algorithms used for handling sensitive information. What can I do until Qlik Replicate November 2023 is compliant? Qlik has two major releases which are already compliant with FIPS. Use either Qlik Replicate November 2022 and Qlik Replicate May 2023. For more information, see, for example: FIPS compliance | Qlik Replicate Help, May 2023

articles.title: Qlik Replicate ODBC Task failure: CREATE SCHEMA "CLILIBF"
articles.description: A task using ODBC as a target fails after an upgrade to 2023.5 or later versions: Errors 00001888: 2024-09-09T10:31:56:332057 [TARGET_LOAD ]E: Failed (retcode -1) to execute statement: CREATE SCHEMA "CLILIBF" [1022502] (ar_odbc_stmt.c:5082) 00001888:…
articles.text: A task using ODBC as a target fails after an upgrade to 2023.5 or later versions: Errors 00001888: 2024-09-09T10:31:56:332057 [TARGET_LOAD ]E: Failed (retcode -1) to execute statement: CREATE SCHEMA "CLILIBF" [1022502] (ar_odbc_stmt.c:5082) 00001888: 2024-09-09T10:31:56:332057 [TARGET_LOAD ]E: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 42000 NativeError: -552 Message: [IBM][System i Access ODBC Driver][DB2 for i5/OS]SQL0552 - Not authorized to CREATE DATABASE. [1022502] (ar_odbc_stmt.c:5090) Before the upgrade, the tasks may have encountered the same error but could be run using a Full Load. Environment Qlik Replicate ODBC DB2 iSERIES as target Resolution To resolve the issue, we will modify an Internal Parameter to the endpoints settings, as well as set a provider syntax . Add the Internal Parameter : Go to the Endpoint connection Switch to the Advanced tab Click Internal Parameters Modify the Parameter: additionalConnectionProperties The old value should be DSN=TGT_PPCPROD If no parameter exists, create it. Add the new value: DSN=TGT_PPCPROD; DBQ=CLILIBF This tells the ODBC driver that any references to table names without an explicit schema name should be resolved in schema CLILIBF. Add the provider syntax Go to the Endpoint connection Switch to the Advanced tab Locate Provider Syntax and add the value GenericWithoutSchema This indicates to the endpoint to disregard schema information, which is the cause of the error. Cause Replicate Upgrade. Oracle to ODBC(iSeries) on 2023.5 will not do a Full Load. Internal Investigation ID(s) QB-29117

articles.title: Qlik Replicate on Linux: High System Memory Usage
articles.description: When Qlik Replicate runs on a newly provisioned Linux server, the system memory usage is abnormally high and reaches critical thresholds.
articles.text: When Qlik Replicate runs on a newly provisioned Linux server, the system memory usage is abnormally high and reaches critical thresholds. Resolution To resolve the issue, reduce or disable huge page allocation by updating the kernel parameter: vm.nr_hugepages = 0 To make it persistent across reboots, update /etc/sysctl.conf . Then apply the change by " sudo sysctl -p " Cause The issue is related to the Linux kernel parameter vm.nr_hugepages , which defines the number of huge pages (typically 2 MB each) that are pre-allocated in memory. In this case, the system was configured with: vm.nr_hugepages = 24629 This reserves approximately 48 GB of memory (2M * 24629) for huge pages, significantly reducing the amount of available memory for other processes. If too many huge pages are reserved, the system may run low on regular memory pages, leading to performance degradation or instability. Internal Investigation ID(s) 00352619 Environment Qlik Replicate, all versions Linux Server, all supported versions

articles.title: Qlik Replicate ORA-03113 Error
articles.description: The Qlik Replicate log reads: 00008260: 2021-12-08T10:31:08 [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]I: ORA-03113: end-of-file on communication channel Process ID: 14794 Session ID: 268 Serial number: 30476 [1022305] (oracle_endpoint_unload.c:1126) Environment Qlik Replicate…
articles.text: The Qlik Replicate log reads: 00008260: 2021-12-08T10:31:08 [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]I: ORA-03113: end-of-file on communication channel Process ID: 14794 Session ID: 268 Serial number: 30476 [1022305] (oracle_endpoint_unload.c:1126) Environment Qlik Replicate ORA-03113: end-of-file on communication error means that the connection with the Oracle source database fails and we are unable to send or receive more events. This can happen for several reasons: The server process servicing the client connection died unexpectedly, or the network communication between the Qlik Replicate server and the Oracle server was interrupted A firewall rule closed a connection due to a timeout (low activity between Oracle and Qlik Replicate). The Oracle database was not online when the error was logged Resolution Qlik Replicate works in a mode that is aware of the batches being processed by each component Source, Sorter and Target, meaning there is no need to worry about data being lost because of this error. This is an environment issue that Qlik Replicate treats as a recoverable error. During CDC it will resume replicating the data from where it left off after the connection is reestablished. A Full Load cannot be resumed and has to start over. How to troubleshoot and address the issue: Check the Oracle Alert log at the time of the issue, see if any trace files were written, and then follow up with your DBA or Oracle Support for root cause analysis. A patch might be available from Oracle for the issue. ert log at the time of the issue, see if any trace files were written, and then follow up with your DBA or Oracle Support for root cause analysis. A patch might be available from Oracle for the issue. Also see Oracle's documentation on this error: ORA-03113 - Database Error Messages (oracle.com) A possible solution would be to add the following line to your SQLNET.ORA file: SQLNET.INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 0 Along with adding the enable=broken parameter to the tnsnames.ora file, which will cause SQLNet to use keep-alive packets: ORCL_REPLICATE = (DESCRIPTION = (ENABLE=BROKEN) (ADDRESS_LIST = (ADDRESS = (PROTOCOL = TCP) (HOST = oracle_server.company.com)(PORT = 1521)) ) (CONNECT_DATA = (SERVICE_NAME = orcl) ) )

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Oracle Source End point TNS Error TNS:listener was not given the SERVICE_NAME in CONNECT_DATA
articles.description: Configuring an Oracle task fails with the below source endpoint error: SYS-E-HTTPFAIL, ORA-12504: TNS:listener was not given the SERVICE_NAME in CONNECT_DATA.

If you are using a service name, check the connect descriptor corresponding to the service name in TNSNAMES.ORA has a SERVICE_NAME or SID component in the CONNECT_DATA Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Oracle Source Redo Log with Sequence not found error when DEST_ID is 32
articles.description: Going to retrieve archived REDO log with sequence 2056016, thread 1 but fails REDO log with a sequence not found error . The Archived Redo Log has Primary Oracle DB as DEST_ID 1 and the Standby DEST_ID 32 pointing to the correct location.
articles.text: Going to retrieve archived REDO log with sequence 2056016, thread 1 but fails REDO log with a sequence not found error . The Archived Redo Log has Primary Oracle DB as DEST_ID 1 and the Standby DEST_ID 32 pointing to the correct location. Environment Qlik Replicate Release 2022.11 previous versions Resolution Cannot use DEST_ID greater than 31 for Primary or Standby Oracle Redo Log locations in prior releases of Replicate 2022.11. The new 2023.5 SR03 supports DEST_ID 32 Cause Qlik Replicate 2022.11 only supported the DEST_ID 0 through 31 Related Content 2023.5 SR03 https://files.qlik.com/url/QR_2023_5_PR03 Internal Investigation ID(s) JIRA RECOB-7509

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Oracle Source Task hangs without failures or errors logged
articles.description: A Qlik Replicate Oracle Source task is not replicating correctly. No errors are logged and the task may appear to be in a running state. You may notice the Last modified date lagging behind.
articles.text: A Qlik Replicate Oracle Source task is not replicating correctly. No errors are logged and the task may appear to be in a running state. You may notice the Last modified date lagging behind. Reviewing logs may show [ASSERTION ]W: Cannot parse a Log Record, continuation. Problematic entry #X. Offset Y. Record data length Z Environment Qlik Replicate Oracle Source The file system that holds the online REDO log (usually a Linux file system or NFS also seen on Solaris and AIX) platforms will cache the Online REDO logs , Oracle writes these files in “direct” mode and does not trigger the refresh of the system cache accordingly. Qlik Replicate can not read the REDOs in “direct “mode because it has no agent running on the DB server. So when replicate reads them, it will read old versions of the REDO logs (for example replicate might ask for the content of a REDO Log with sequence 104, but get the content of REDO log sequence 100, from before the last log switch). To be able to read the REDOs in “regular” mode in a reliable way, It is necessary to evict the REDOs from the system cache periodically. We refer to this internally as the ‘caching problem’. This problem exposes itself in many different ways. Resolution From the Qlik Replicate side there is unfortunately not a lot we can do. A lot depends on the file system the customer uses for redo logs. If this is not mounted for direct IO (and thus buffered by the file/system cache) we can have this problem. Three options can be applied to mitigate this: The first option requires changes to file system settings and placing the (online) redo log files on an unbuffered file share. Alternatively, set Qlik Replicate to Use archived redo logs only ( if business requirements (latency) allow that). system settings and placing the (online) redo log files on an unbuffered file share. Alternatively, set Qlik Replicate to Use archived redo logs only ( if business requirements (latency) allow that). Go to your Source Endpoint Connection Go to the Advanced tab Check Use archived redo logs only The second workaround is to frequently flush the cached redo log data. This way Qlik Replicate will read the right blocks. The third workaround is to enable Oracle LogMiner . Go to your Source Endpoint Connection Go to the Advanced tab Check Oracle LogMiner

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Postgres as a target disconnect: TARGET_APPLY server closed the connection unexpectedly
articles.description: The Qlik Replicate logs may report the following error on Target Apply: [TARGET_APPLY ]E: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 08S01 NativeError: 35 Message: server closed the connection unexpectedly Resolution Add the Internal Parameter…
articles.text: The Qlik Replicate logs may report the following error on Target Apply: [TARGET_APPLY ]E: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 08S01 NativeError: 35 Message: server closed the connection unexpectedly Resolution Add the Internal Parameter additionalConnectionProperties ( a ) to the Postgres Target endpoint and provide the following two ODBC parameters ( b 😞 KeepaliveTime=60; KeepaliveInterval=1; See Qlik Replicate: How to set Internal Parameters and what are they for? for detailed instructions on how to add an Internal Parameter. Cause If Qlik is replicating across networks that transit cloud infrastructure or have any type of firewall device, the database connection options must enable a TCP keepalive setting or certain scenarios will cause idle connections to age-out. In one of the scenarios, data pipeline loads create large updates that must be inserted on the target. These inserts take time, long enough for Qlik's sessions to age-out idle across the intermediate network devices. This required setting the mentioned flags for the Postgres ODBC driver. Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate postgres source - ERROR: all replication slots are in use
articles.description: I encountered the following error: Creating replication slot 'postie_test_pk_00016394_5281ce4c_6304_2b4d_9a64_86e5f359f324' failed. wal_slot_create(...) - Unable to create slot 'postie_test_pk_00016394_5281ce4c_6304_2b4d_9a64_86e5f359f324' (on execute(...)…
articles.text: I encountered the following error: Creating replication slot 'postie_test_pk_00016394_5281ce4c_6304_2b4d_9a64_86e5f359f324' failed. wal_slot_create(...) - Unable to create slot 'postie_test_pk_00016394_5281ce4c_6304_2b4d_9a64_86e5f359f324' (on execute(...) phase) RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 53400 NativeError: 1 Message: ERROR: all replication slots are in use; Error while executing the query Failed (retcode -1) to execute statement: 'SELECT lsn FROM pg_create_logical_replication_slot('postie_test_pk_00016394_5281ce4c_6304_2b4d_9a64_86e5f359f324', 'test_decoding')' Steps to investigate: 1. Check on postgres source if another process is using all of the replication slots. Please be advised these could be other Replicate task or business processes so proceed with caution. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/30854961/how-to-delete-replication-slot-in-postgres-9-4 https://hevodata.com/learn/postgresql-replication-slots/ 2. Try increasing the max_replication_slots so Replicate can attempt to use another slot. This is a parameter set in postgresql.conf file. The default number of replication slots is 10. Once 10 slots are consumed, even if the slots are not actively in use, a new task cannot start. The task error is treated as recoverable and will cause the task to attempt to start indefinitely. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-replication.html Once I freed up the slots (from #1 above), I was able to run the Replicate task. Environment Qlik Replicate The information in this article is provided as-is and to be used at own discretion. Depending on tool(s) used, customization(s), and/or other factors ongoing support on the solution below may not be provided by Qlik Support.

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Primary key with NULL values in CT tables due to Oracle October 2023 patch
articles.description: When Qlik Replicate runs in CDC mode and CT tables are enabled, primary keys are replicated as null values in the CT tables. Base tables are not affected by this.
articles.text: When Qlik Replicate runs in CDC mode and CT tables are enabled, primary keys are replicated as null values in the CT tables. Base tables are not affected by this. The Oracle patch from the 19th of October 2023 changed the redo log format around how they log before images. Qlik has issued a patch (2023.5 SP5) to read the new format correctly. Resolution A fix has been provided in Qlik Replicate 2023.5 SP5 and 2023.11 SP1. Download and install one of the provided patches: Qlik Replicate 2023.5 SP05 Public download link: https://files.qlik.com/url/qr2023050701sp05 (expires 5/31/2024) Once this download link expires, a patch will be made available on the Qlik download page. Qlik Enterprise Manager 2023.5 SP05 Included if you are using Qlik Enterprise Manager to match the version with Qlik Replicate. Public download link: https://files.qlik.com/url/qem2023050614sp05 (expires 5/31/2024) Once this download link expires, a patch will be made available on the Qlik download page. Environment Qlik Replicate May, version 2023.5.0.516 and earlier. Qlik Replicate 2023.11.0.159 (GA)

articles.title: Qlik Replicate R4Z: Understanding ECSA memory allocation for each DB2z CDC service
articles.description: The purpose of this article is to explain the ESCA (Extended Shared Common Area) memory allocation in a z/OS logical partition with an active Qlik R4Z component for DB2 CDC.
articles.text: The purpose of this article is to explain the ESCA (Extended Shared Common Area) memory allocation in a z/OS logical partition with an active Qlik R4Z component for DB2 CDC. What drives how much ECSA memory is required by each CDC service? Qlik Replicate R4Z mechanism (Replicate for zSeries) uses ECSA as follows: For each defined replicate “service”, there is: ANCHOR - 56 bytes Maxsessions (default 32) x session control block, using about 260 bytes each Each active session will use: The configured IFI buffer size + (an aux buffer, 260 bytes of miscellaneous info) + (filter list) Where filter list = 260 bytes + 4 * number of tables With TRACE level task logging for SOURCE_CAPTURE component, one can find this in two messaged from the UDTF, as follows: 00031324: 2022-06-24T19:18:51:745788 [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]T: R4DB2: Updated EXT buffer length 260 RC 0 (r4z2util.c:1877 (db2z_ifi_api.c:994) 00031324: 2022-06-24T19:18:55:960285 [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]T: R4DB2: Updated EXT buffer length 272 RC 0 (r4z2util.c:1877 (db2z_ifi_api.c:994) Here the 12 byte increase is from 2 user tables plus SYSIBM.SYSTABLES , which is always included in the list. The IFI Buffer size is also shown in the following message: 00031324: 2022-06-24T19:18:51:741801 [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]I: R4DB2: IFI Buffer size 256 KB . (r4zudf.c:352 (db2z_ifi_api.c:994) The number of tables in the task and the IFI buffer size are the two big variable. It’s not recommended to configure for more than a 256 kb IFI buffer, but maximum number of tables could be as high as 50,000 or 200 kb for the filter list. This is a possible maximum of more than 456 kb per active task, Although the experience shows that it is very unlikely that any task would have 50,000 tables and even less likely that more than one task would have that many.' Environment: Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate reading from DB2i Source getting W:  Alternate backup file
articles.description: Qlik Replicate reading from DB2i Source getting W: Alternate backup file Qlik Replicate is reading from the DB2i Source environment and the data that is being written to the Target is showing the RRN column which is defined as the Primary Key being duplicated…
articles.text: Qlik Replicate reading from DB2i Source getting W: Alternate backup file Qlik Replicate is reading from the DB2i Source environment and the data that is being written to the Target is showing the RRN column which is defined as the Primary Key being duplicated in the Source. Resolution The notification you are getting about the backup not existing is most likely because you have a notification set for ‘any warning’. While this is not an issue you will get this message. You can reduce how many times you get this warning by setting the internal parameter ‘alternateBackupWaitForFile’ to a higher value then 10 seconds. Cause The alternate backup wait for a file has the default of 10 set. To resolve the issue to have the Warning not be shown would be to increase the parameter using the internal parameter. Environment Qlik Replicate all versions Related Content Setting advanced connection properties

articles.title: Qlik Replicate reading from DB2i Source has RRN values being the same as already processed
articles.description: Qlik Replicate is reading from the DB2i Source environment and the data that is being written to the Target is showing the RRN column which is defined as the Primary Key is being duplicated in the Source.
articles.text: Qlik Replicate is reading from the DB2i Source environment and the data that is being written to the Target is showing the RRN column which is defined as the Primary Key is being duplicated in the Source. Resolution The issue as it relates to the RRN value from the DB2i Source environment is due to the definition of the File/Table on the Source. The REUSEDLT(*YES) on the Create Physical File (CRTPF) for this Table is setup to REUSE the RRN should be confirmed if this is set as this will recycle the RRN to be reused. Cause There is a setting on the DB2i File Definition of Table REUSEDLT(*YES) this allows the DB environment to reuse the RRN that may have been used already which would cause the behavior. Environment Qlik Replicate all versions Related Content https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/i/7.2?topic=options-reusing-deleted-records

Environment Qlik Replicate Qlik Replicate 2021.11 Higher The Oracle Source Endpoint will need to be set up as you will need to add the below internal parameter to point to the Standby Node (thread) Replicate will read from. articles.text: Qlik Replicate generates a Repcmd.log file frequently (such as once per minute). The files are less than 1KB large. Resolution Review if you have a script scheduled at the frequency you are seeing the files being generated (such as every minute). For every Repctl command that is run, a Repcmd.log file will be created. This is working as designed. Cause A script scheduled to run once every minute. Internal Investigation ID(s) 66340 Environment Qlik Replicate, any version on any platform

articles.title: Qlik Replicate reports changes are not being captured error
articles.description: The warning changes are not being captured may be caused by 2 things: Reason 1 Valid scenario, where parent/log stream tasks actually did not receive any data from the source, for example, if the changes currently happening on the source are not related to…
articles.text: The warning changes are not being captured may be caused by 2 things: Reason 1 Valid scenario, where parent/log stream tasks actually did not receive any data from the source, for example, if the changes currently happening on the source are not related to the tables in the task. You can confirm this by verifying that there is no data discrepancy between source and target. Reason 2 Error scenario, where parent/log stream task encountered an issue and parent/log stream task continues to run without throwing an error. Check the staging task if there is an error during the same time frame when you received the warning on the replication task. For example, the staging task has stopped writing data to the log stream files for some reason. For the second scenario, please open a support case for assistance. Environment: Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate running on Windows using TLS Versions 1.1 and 1.2
articles.description: Qlik Replicate may connect to an AWS Target S3 Bucket Endpoint with either TLS 1.1 or 1.2. As TLS 1.1 is outdated, it may be necessary to remove it from the Qlik Replicate host machine.
articles.text: Qlik Replicate may connect to an AWS Target S3 Bucket Endpoint with either TLS 1.1 or 1.2. As TLS 1.1 is outdated, it may be necessary to remove it from the Qlik Replicate host machine. Qlik Replicate must be upgraded to at least the 2022.11 (November 2022) version. For instructions on how to disable TLS 1.1 and set 1.2 to default, consult Update to enable TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 as default secure protocols in WinHTTP in Windows | Microsoft . Related Content If you disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 on the Qlik Replicate Sever then an upgrade to Qlik Replicate 2022.11 or later is required. Qlik Replicate 7.0 still supports TLS 1.0 and 1.1 (as well as 1.2). Environment Qlik Replicate 7.0

articles.description: SAP Cluster Tables has missing data in the Target during CDC process. Environment Qlik Replicate 2023.5 Resolution Apply the latest Service Release for Replicate 2023.5 SP03.
articles.text: SAP Cluster Tables has missing data in the Target during CDC process. Environment Qlik Replicate 2023.5 Resolution Apply the latest Service Release for Replicate 2023.5 SP03. https://files.qlik.com/url/QR_2023_5_PR03 Workaround: Start the task using the Advanced Run Options... and start from the timestamp at which the data loss was noticed. As long as the transactions logs are available, the issue will be resolved. Go to the task Click the drop-down arrow next to Run Choose Advanced Run Options... Set the Date and Time to the UTC timestamp on the Qlik Replicate server and at the point at which the data loss was observed Cause Product Defect ID: RECOB-7506 Related Content Using SAP Application (DB) as a source

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SAP Application DB upgrade DB2 LUW: Bad data in target
articles.description: The SAP Application DB Source endpoint database was upgraded. Data is now not in the correct format when being processed to the target endpoint. Resolution Due to the backend DB2 LUW Database being upgraded the setting for the DB is set to Non-Unicode.
articles.text: The SAP Application DB Source endpoint database was upgraded. Data is now not in the correct format when being processed to the target endpoint. Resolution Due to the backend DB2 LUW Database being upgraded the setting for the DB is set to Non-Unicode. The option is not checked on the SAP Application DB Source Endpoint under the Advanced Tab. Resolve the issue by checking the Non-Unicode SAP system checkbox. Cause Due to the DB2 LUW Upgrade from previous version to the new version they did not enable Unicode on the Database as it has been set to Non-Unicode SAP System. Environment Qlik Replicate Related Content Setting advanced properties

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SAP Hana Source Oracle Target CDC its replicated as empty string
articles.description: During the initial load, if a field is empty in SAP, it correctly replicates as a space in Oracle. However, during CDC, it is being replicated as an empty string, which is incorrect.
articles.text: During the initial load, if a field is empty in SAP, it correctly replicates as a space in Oracle. However, during CDC, it is being replicated as an empty string, which is incorrect. Resolution Correcting this behavior requires the Internal Parameter alwaysReplaceEmptyStrings to be disabled on the Oracle Target. alwaysReplaceEmptyStrings is enabled by default. Go to the Oracle Target Endpoint connection Switch to the Advanced tab Click Internal Parameters Search alwaysReplaceEmptyStrings and untick the checkbox For more information on Internal Parameters, see Qlik Replicate: How to set Internal Parameters and what are they for? Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SAP Hana Trigger Base Backend DB Endpoint using Full Record Mode with SAP Application DB Source Endpoint
articles.description: The new SAP Hana trigger based backend DB Endpoint, used with the SAP Application DB Endpoint, fails when using the new Full Record Mode (V4) triggers.
articles.text: The new SAP Hana trigger based backend DB Endpoint, used with the SAP Application DB Endpoint, fails when using the new Full Record Mode (V4) triggers. The logged error: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: S1000 NativeError: 362 Message: [SAP AG][LIBODBCHDB DLL][HDBODBC] General error;362 invalid schema name: R4S - SCHEMA_NAME: line 1 col 15 (at pos 14) [1022502] Failed to get table R4S - SCHEMA.TABLE_NAME definition [1022500] Resolution Upgrade to Qlik Replicate 2024.11 SP05 or higher. Cause An update was necessary to Qlik Replicate due to how the table list is being captured in the SAP Source Endpoint. Internal Investigation ID(s) RECOB-10089 Environment Qlik Replicate versions before 2024.11 SP05

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SAP HANA trigger base fails to do Insert from to the cdc_log Table
articles.description: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: S1000 NativeError: 260 Message: [SAP AG][LIBODBCHDB DLL][HDBODBC] General error;260 invalid column name: APPLICATION_USER There are two types of trigger based replication methods with SAP HANA Source endpoints: from Log table or…
articles.text: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: S1000 NativeError: 260 Message: [SAP AG][LIBODBCHDB DLL][HDBODBC] General error;260 invalid column name: APPLICATION_USER There are two types of trigger based replication methods with SAP HANA Source endpoints: from Log table or from CDC artifacts . For the former (which is related to the error above), by selecting ' Use log table ' from the SAP HANA Source advanced tab, it will generate the attrep_cdc_log table, which Qlik Replicate can read changes from. When this option is enabled, during the task, Qlik Replicate copies the changes from the attrep_cdc_changes table to the attrep_cdc_log table. This is the preferred method of working (and, in future versions, will be the only method of working) as it significantly reduces latency. Issue: If you select ' Use Log Table ' setting, it will not drop the existing changes_cdc Table, and the version of the triggers can be invalid. The change_cdc and cdc_log Table would not be in sync and thus throw the Column error. Resolution Steps to clean up and recreate the changes_cdc and cdc_log Tables: Stop the tasks Manually drop attrep_cdc_changes and attrep_cdc_log and triggers. Manually drop triggers. You can use SAP HANA Studio and run the following queries to check what triggers are installed. Or you can look at the C:\Program Files\Attunity\Replicate\data\tasks\SAP HANA Test\scripts as this is where the SQL is generated for the Tables and triggers. Note the version of triggers on the client will need to match their environment. \Attunity\Replicate\data\tasks\SAP HANA Test\scripts as this is where the SQL is generated for the Tables and triggers. Note the version of triggers on the client will need to match their environment. Examples: DROP TRIGGER "SCHEMA"."attrep_cdc_v1_29834822_I_VBAK_29835233"; DROP TRIGGER "SCHEMA"."attrep_cdc_v1_29834822_U_VBAK_29835233"; DROP TRIGGER "SCHEMA"."attrep_cdc_v1_29834822_D_VBAK_29835233" DROP TABLE "SCHEMA"."attrep_cdc_log"; DROP TABLE "SCHEMA"."attrep_cdc_changes"; Reload tables Cause If you had set up the SAP HANA originally without the ' Use Log Table ' for the Trigger Based setup, it would not have created the cdc_log Table. If you configure it after the task has started, it does not drop the existing change_log Table. Thus, the columns would not match as the Column Name APPLICATION_USER is defined in the change_log and not the cdc_log Table. Environment Qlik Replicate All Versions Related Content Qlik Replicate and SAP HANA Trigger based CDC

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SAP Hana Trigger Full Record Mode supports SAP Application DB Source only
articles.description: If you are using the SAP Application Endpoint for CDC processing and want to implement the new Full Record Mode feature with the Trigger-based endpoint, you will also need to convert the existing SAP Application Endpoint to use the SAP Application DB…
articles.text: If you are using the SAP Application Endpoint for CDC processing and want to implement the new Full Record Mode feature with the Trigger-based endpoint, you will also need to convert the existing SAP Application Endpoint to use the SAP Application DB Endpoint. In Qlik Replicate 2025.5 (and later versions): Qlik Replicate 2025.5 exposes the setting directly in the endpoint Advanced tab. Go to the SAP Hana Source Endpoint Switch to the Advanced tab Set Record Mode to Full Record The Endpoint now has the SAP HANA source endpoint defined as the Backend DB with Version 4 Trigger in Full Record Mode enabled. In Qlik Replicate 2024.11 SP04 to the latest 2024.11 SP: Set the Backend database to the SAP Hana Trigger Based Endpoint Switch to the Advanced tab and set: CDC Mode: Trigger-based CDC Trigger mode: Primary key only Trigger-based mode: Log Table Check Create CDC artifacts Now set sapHanaFullRecord in More Options Go to More Options in the Endpoint settings Add sapHanaFullRecord and set it to On Save the Endpoint The SAP Hana Endpoint has Full Record Mode (version 4) enabled, which requires a Full Reload of the Source to move to this new mode. Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SAP ODP CDS View not processing Updates done in SAP
articles.description: When replicating a CDS View the Updates are being processed as Inserts not Updates. In SAP the CDS views delta with UPSERT and SAP capture INSERT and UPDATE both as one operation which is treated as INSERT.
articles.text: When replicating a CDS View the Updates are being processed as Inserts not Updates. In SAP the CDS views delta with UPSERT and SAP capture INSERT and UPDATE both as one operation which is treated as INSERT. If you have a SAP login you can look up SAP Note 3300238 for more information as shown below: SAP Note 3300238 - ABAP CDS CDC: ODQ_CHANGEMODE not showing proper status forcreation Component: BW-WHM-DBA-ODA (SAP Business Warehouse > Data Warehouse Management > Data Basis >Operational Data Provider for ABAP CDS, HANA & BW), Version: 4, Released On: 19.01.2024 Resolution This is working as expected. It is the designed behavior of the CDC logic. For both insert and update, ODQ_CHANGEMODE = U and ODQ_ENTITYCNTR = 1. The CDC-delta logic is designed as UPSERT-logic. This means a DB-INSERT (or create) or a DB-UPDATE both get the ODQ_CHANGEMODE = U and ODQ_ENTITYCNTR = 1. It's not possible to distinguish in CDC-delta between Create and Update. Environment Qlik Replicate SAP S/4HANA SAP BW/4HANA

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SAP ODP Source Endpoint common problems with causes
articles.description: Common issues with SAP Operational Data Provisioning ( ODP ) in combination with Qlik Replicate can arise from both the SAP backend and the integration layer .
articles.text: Common issues with SAP Operational Data Provisioning ( ODP ) in combination with Qlik Replicate can arise from both the SAP backend and the integration layer . This article offers a breakdown of the most frequent problems and their causes: ODP Context Misconfiguration Missing or Inactive Subscriptions CDS Views Not Supporting UPDATE ODQMON Shows 0 Rows ODP Extractor Not Delta-Enabled Authorization Issues ODP Queue Corruption or Locking Java or SDK Issues on the Qlik Replicate Server Incorrect Task Configuration in Replicate ODP Context Misconfiguration Symptoms : No data or incorrect data pulled. Cause : Wrong ODP context (such as SAPI, CDS, BW, ABAP_CDS) used in the endpoint configuration. Fix : Confirm the correct context for the data source in SAP and match it in Qlik Replicate. Missing or Inactive Subscriptions Symptoms : No data appears in ODQMON or Qlik Replicate. Cause : The subscription (such as QLIK_REPLICATE) is not created or is not active. Fix : Check ODQMON for the subscription status. Re-run the task or reinitialize the subscription. CDS Views Not Supporting UPDATE Symptoms : CDC is not capturing updates. Cause : CDS Views via ODP do not support UPDATE operations. Fix : This is a SAP limitation. Consider redesigning the data model or using a different source. ODQMON Shows 0 Rows Symptoms : A task runs, but no data is captured. Cause : No delta records available or incorrect delta initialization. Fix : Verify that delta is enabled in the source and the extractor is correctly configured. Check with your SAP Basis team if necessary. ODP Extractor Not Delta-Enabled Symptoms : CDC fails, or only full load works. Cause : The extractor (such as CDS View or a custom extractor) is not delta-enabled. Fix : Use a delta-enabled extractor or modify the extractor logic in SAP. Authorization Issues Symptoms : Connection errors or missing data. ch as CDS View or a custom extractor) is not delta-enabled. Fix : Use a delta-enabled extractor or modify the extractor logic in SAP. Authorization Issues Symptoms : Connection errors or missing data. Cause : The SAP user used by Qlik Replicate lacks the required roles or authorizations. Fix : Verify the user has access to: ODQMON SM37 Relevant CDS Views or extractors RFC and ODP access ODP Queue Corruption or Locking Symptoms : Jobs hang or fail in ODQMON. Cause : Queue corruption or locks from previous failed jobs. Fix : Clear or reset the queue in ODQMON. May require SAP Basis support. Java or SDK Issues on the Qlik Replicate Server Symptoms : Endpoint fails to connect or crashes. Cause : Missing or incompatible Java SDK used by Qlik Replicate's internal endpoint server. Fix : Reinstall or update the Java SDK and verify compatibility with your Qlik Replicate version. Incorrect Task Configuration in Replicate Symptoms : A task fails or pulls incorrect data. Cause : Wrong object name, context, or load mode selected. Fix : Double-check task settings, especially: Object name (such as Z_VBAP_JW$F) Example: Table Object or Name in Task Load mode (Full Load vs. CDC) Endpoint server status Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate scheduled jobs won't start after Qlik Replicate upgrade
articles.description: After upgrading Qlik Replicate may cause scheduled jobs to fail due to changes in the Scheduler functionality. Example error: [UTILITIES ]E: Command request 'RESUMETASK_REQ' (55) cannot be found.
articles.text: After upgrading Qlik Replicate may cause scheduled jobs to fail due to changes in the Scheduler functionality. Example error: [UTILITIES ]E: Command request 'RESUMETASK_REQ' (55) cannot be found. [1020111] (scheduler.c:270) In this specific example, the scheduled job didn't run because it had selected the option to "RESUME TASK", which has been removed in more recent versions of Replicate. Environment Qlik Replicate Example: Upgrade from 7.0 to 2021.1 Resolution A quick solution is to export/import the repository, b elow are the steps: Under Replicate server -> Logging -> Log File Management -> Uncheck any Log roll over you might have Replicate Server -> Scheduler -> Take a screenshot here as you'll need to recreate the jobs Disable all the scheduled jobs Export repository by going on cmd to Replicate bin/ folder and running: repctl exportrepository It's going to create a JSON file called Replication_Definition.json under Replicate/data/imports , please backup this file by renaming it Edit it with notepad++ and empty the scheduler section, it should be like this: "scheduler": { }, Save it and make sure it's called Replication_Definition.json Import repository by running under Replicate /bin folder: repctl importrepository json_file=Replication_Definition If you have a custom location of the data folder, make sure you specify it by adding the flag -d before the json_file. Recreate the scheduled jobs Test the schedule

articles.title: Qlik Replicate server crashes with "Cancel async command failed" when connecting to a Teradata source or target endpoint and tasks do not start
articles.description: Using Test Connection when testing a connection to a Teradata source or target endpoint leads to the Qlik Replicate server crashing. Any tasks using the Teradata source endpoint or Teradata target endpoint cannot be started.
articles.text: Using Test Connection when testing a connection to a Teradata source or target endpoint leads to the Qlik Replicate server crashing. Any tasks using the Teradata source endpoint or Teradata target endpoint cannot be started. Errors: ERROR: check_async_command_complete failed ERROR: Cancel async command failed. The issue occurs only with Qlik Replicate hosted on Linux. Windows installs are not affected. Environment: Qlik Replicate 2023.11 GA (2023.11.0.159) Teradata TTU and ODBC version 17.20 (builds 17.20.04.00 - 17.20.21.00) Teradata Server 17.20 Resolution: Fix: The issue is caused by a compatibility conflict between ODBC Driver Manager and Kerberos libraries. No permanent fix is yet available. Qlik is actively working on providing a solution. Review the release notes for QB-23862. Workaround: If at all possible, run Qlik Replicate 2022.11. This version is unaffected by QB-23862. If Kerberos is not used, rename one of Kerberos-related .so files: Run: cd /opt/attunity/replicate/lib Run: mv libgssapi_krb5.so.2 libgssapi_krb5.so.2ORG Restart the Qlik Replicate service Cause & Internal Investigation ID(s): QB-23862, #00129279, #00128123 Compatibility conflict between ODBC Driver Manager and Kerberos libraries. articles.title: Qlik Replicate Server starts and then immediately stops: Faulting module name: KERNELBASE.dll, version: 10.0.14393.5582
articles.description: The Qlik Replicate Server fails to start properly. It starts and immediately stops again. The Windows Application Event logs read: Faulting module name: KERNELBASE.dll, version: 10.0.14393.5582 Resolution The error message indicates that the service user does…
articles.text: The Qlik Replicate Server fails to start properly. It starts and immediately stops again. The Windows Application Event logs read: Faulting module name: KERNELBASE.dll, version: 10.0.14393.5582 Resolution The error message indicates that the service user does not have the correct permissions. Option One: Add the service account running the Qlik Replicate Server service to the Windows Local Administrator Group . Option Two : Configure the service account as per Running Replicate under a different account Environment Replicate 2021 and above

articles.description: Qlik Replicate service crashes with Snowflake ODBC driver 2.25.11 After installing Snowflake ODBC driver 2.25.11 and restarting the server, the Qlik Replicate service crashes whenever a Snowflake endpoint connection is created.
articles.text: Qlik Replicate service crashes with Snowflake ODBC driver 2.25.11 After installing Snowflake ODBC driver 2.25.11 and restarting the server, the Qlik Replicate service crashes whenever a Snowflake endpoint connection is created. Resolution: Revert to an earlier version of the Snowflake ODBC driver. According to the release notes of the Snowflake ODBC driver, the crash problem was addressed in version 2.25.6. See ODBC Driver Release Notes . To address the crash issue observed in the Snowflake ODBC driver version 2.25.11, we recommend opening a support ticket with the Snowflake vendor. articles.title: Qlik Replicate services fail to start with error Cannot access log.key file
articles.description: After an upgrade of Qlik Replicate, the Qlik Replicate service may fail to start with error: error cannot access log.key file Resolution We have introduced log file encryption beginning with the 2021 releases of Qlik Replicate.
articles.text: After an upgrade of Qlik Replicate, the Qlik Replicate service may fail to start with error: error cannot access log.key file Resolution We have introduced log file encryption beginning with the 2021 releases of Qlik Replicate. If the Qlik Replicate services are run with a service account which does not have permission to read the required log.key file, the service will fail to start. To resolve, choose to either : Follow the instructions as per Changing the Qlik Replicate Server Service account and give the account all the required permissions Give the current service account full local server admin permissions by adding it to the Administrator group. Related Content: How to Decrypt Qlik Replicate Verbose Task Log Files Environment Qlik Replicate 2021 and later versions

articles.title: Qlik Replicate services fail to start: The service did not respond to the start or control request in a timely fashion.
articles.description: Qlik Replicate services (Qlik Replicate Server or Qlik Replicate UI Service) may fail to start after an upgrade. Starting the services fails with: The Qlik Replicate Server service failed to start due to the following error: The service did not respond to the…
articles.text: Qlik Replicate services (Qlik Replicate Server or Qlik Replicate UI Service) may fail to start after an upgrade. Starting the services fails with: The Qlik Replicate Server service failed to start due to the following error: The service did not respond to the start or control request in a timely fashion. A timeout was reached (30000 milliseconds) while waiting for the Qlik Replicate Server service to connect. The Windows Event logs show: Description: the process was terminated due to an unhandled exception. Exception Info: System.IO.IOException Resolution Verify if the drive Qlik Replicate is installed on is managed by, for example, BitLocker . Disable BitLocker or set up exceptions and start the services again. Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate set to apply prefix replacement to archived redo logs only but uses online redo logs settings as well
articles.description: Qlik Replicate is set to apply prefix replacement to archived redo logs only and specifies file-level access to archive location , yet continues to use the online redo logs and may fail a task as per the following error: Failed to open Redo log…
articles.text: Qlik Replicate is set to apply prefix replacement to archived redo logs only and specifies file-level access to archive location , yet continues to use the online redo logs and may fail a task as per the following error: Failed to open Redo log '/oracle/serverbackup/origlog/log123.dbf The settings are done correctly, with only Replicate has file-level access to the new archive location checked: Resolution Set the Internal Parameter of useAlternateFolderAlways on the Oracle Source Endpoint: Go to Advanced Click Internal Parameters Add useAlternateFolderAlways and tick the checkbox For more information about Internal Parameters, see Qlik Replicate: How to set Internal Parameters and what are they for? Return to the Advanced tab and set Apply prefix replacement to archived redo logs only Select Replicate has file-level access to the new archive location Save the Endpoint and add all necessary tables to the task Export the task to JSON; see Exporting tasks or details Open the JSON and delete the UseBfile entry: "useBfile": true, Import the modified JSON. Do no make changes to the Endpoint at this stage. Reviewing the Apply prefix replacement to archived redo logs only section now shows both options selected: Replicate has file-level access to the original online location Replicate has file-level access to the new archive location This is a UI glitch. Do not untick the selections. Start the task. Qlik Replicate will now only have file-level access to the new archive location and not use the online location. Disregard the UI glitch. Internal Investigation ID(s) 000014626, 00164729 Environment Qlik Replicate Oracle Source Endpoint

articles.title: Qlik Replicate shows MySQL client out of memory error while reading from a MYSQL source
articles.description: As per this mysql article, the ODBC driver has to use mysql_use_result() to skip out of memory errors: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/out-of-memory.html Here is the ODBC parameters list and we found NO_CACHE is the listed parameter to enable…
articles.text: As per this mysql article, the ODBC driver has to use mysql_use_result() to skip out of memory errors: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/out-of-memory.html Here is the ODBC parameters list and we found NO_CACHE is the listed parameter to enable mysql_use_result() for the MySQL client: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/connector-odbc/en/connector-odbc-configuration-connection-parameters.html You can add NO_CACHE on MySQL endpoint --> Go to MYSQL endpoint-->Advanced-->Additional ODBC connection properties. You can see the affected parameter from the log also as below: 00019392: 2022-03-25T13:27:06:659296 [TASK_MANAGER ]I: Task Id: 7b0f52f9-358a-0a4a-aec2-eee8df5b4a01 (replicationtask.c:3779) 00019392: 2022-03-25T13:27:06:683865 [METADATA_MANAGE ]I: Driver 'MySQL ODBC 8.0 Unicode Driver' is installed and will be used (mysql_endpoint_imp.c:439) 00019392: 2022-03-25T13:27:06:683865 [METADATA_MANAGE ]I: ODBC additional properties = 'NO_CACHE' (mysql_endpoint_imp.c:496) 00019392: 2022-03-25T13:27:06:683865 [METADATA_MANAGE ]I: Connecting to MySQL using ODBC connection string: DRIVER={MySQL ODBC 8.0 Unicode Driver};SERVER=localhost;port=3306;UID=root;DB=;CHARSET=binary;initstmt=SET time_zone='+00:00';Option=74448896; NO_CACHENO_LOCALE=1 ;ENABLE_LOCAL_INFILE=0;sslmode=Preferred;PWD=***; (mysql_endpoint_imp.c:597) Environment Qlik Replicate MYSQL

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Snowflake RSA key-based authentication fails with RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: HY000 NativeError
articles.description: Snowflake has mandated the use of MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) for all users. As a result, traditional password-based authentication is no longer sufficient.
articles.text: Snowflake has mandated the use of MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) for all users. As a result, traditional password-based authentication is no longer sufficient. To bypass MFA for automated processes, the endpoint was configured using RSA key-based authentication (public/private key pair). While the test connection on the Snowflake endpoint succeeds, the actual data replication task consistently fails during the PUT command execution. Inspecting the Snowflake shows the PUT command succeeds, yet Qlik Replicate reports a failure with the following error: "RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: HY000 NativeError: 40 Message: [Snowflake][Snowflake] (40) Failed to upload file" Resolution There are multiple possible root causes and solutions. This article documents two most common scenarios. Firewall Restriction A firewall rule may be blocking Qlik Replicate's file PUT operation to Snowflake's local stage, preventing file upload during bulk load. To resolve Engage your network and security team to review firewall logs and: Confirm whether bulk load traffic (such as large PUT file uploads to Snowflake) is being blocked or restricted. Temporarily allow unrestricted egress to .snowflakecomputing.com and related AWS resources for verification. Proxy Interference or Certificate Trust Issue A proxy server could be interfering with traffic. Alternatively, the SSL certificate may not be trusted by the proxy layer or Snowflake endpoint. ication. Proxy Interference or Certificate Trust Issue A proxy server could be interfering with traffic. Alternatively, the SSL certificate may not be trusted by the proxy layer or Snowflake endpoint. To resolve Verify the Proxy Bypass Configuration: Go to Manage Endpoint Connections Go to the Snowflake Endpoint Go to Advanced In Additional ODBC Connection Properties , ensure the NO_PROXY option is set to bypass the proxy for Snowflake domains: “NO_PROXY=.snowflakecomputing.com,.amazonaws.com” Example: AUTHENTICATOR=SNOWFLAKE_JWT;PRIV_KEY_FILE=D:\QLIKKey\rsa_key.p8;PRIV_KEY_FILE_PWD=123456;role=APP-WS;PROXY=proxy.ibm.local:9595;NO_PROXY=.snowflakecomputing.com,.amazonaws.com Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Snowflake Target Table Schema not respected
articles.description: The defined Target Table Scheme in Qlik Replicate is ignored and the table's native schema is used. Environment Qlik Replicate Snowflake Endpoint Resolution Global rules in Snowflake that uppercase everything will interfere.
articles.text: The defined Target Table Scheme in Qlik Replicate is ignored and the table's native schema is used. Environment Qlik Replicate Snowflake Endpoint Resolution Global rules in Snowflake that uppercase everything will interfere. Such as: Uppercase Schema, Uppercase Table Name, Uppercase Column. When the Target Schema is used in conjunction with the uppercase schema, the Target Schema is ignored. Remove the uppercase schema rule and make sure the target schema is uppercase already.

articles.title: Qlik Replicate Source SAP Hana Log Base Endpoint: Events are not processed in the expected order
articles.description: Using a SAP Hana Source with Log Base as an Endpoint in Qlik Replicate leads to changes processed by CDC being processed out of order. This causes issues on the Target Endpoint.
articles.text: Using a SAP Hana Source with Log Base as an Endpoint in Qlik Replicate leads to changes processed by CDC being processed out of order. This causes issues on the Target Endpoint. Example of the output from the CDC events: select *,"$rowid$" from fkkmako where "$rowid$" in ('88636168','88636198','88636272','88636266','88636245','88636210') Resolution This was caused by defect RECOB-9960, which affected Qlik Replicate 2024.11. Upgrade to Qlik Replicate 2024.11 Build 641 or higher. Internal Investigation ID(s) RECOB-9960 Environment Qlik Replicate 2024.11

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SQL Server source queries fn_dump_dblog vs fn_dblog
articles.description: Qlik Replicate tasks using SQL Servers as a source shows two long running queries on the source database from the internal processes of QLIK.
articles.text: Qlik Replicate tasks using SQL Servers as a source shows two long running queries on the source database from the internal processes of QLIK. See below examples: The longest running queries are SELECT TOP 50000 from sys.fn_dblog and SELECT /*TOP 50000*/ from sys.fn_dump_dblog . The TOP 50000 statement is commented out by the use of ‘/* */’. What is the difference between the 2 queries: SELECT /*TOP 50000*/ from sys.fn_dump_dblog vs SELECT TOP 50000 from sys.fn_dblog By default, the batch size is 50000. To change this, we will configure an internal parameter on your SQL server endpoint: logScanBatchSize . This defines how many TRXs/changes will be collected to a batch. The default is 50K. We know that on slow DBs it might take more time to collect TRXs and therefore to have as close as can to real time, you can try to reduce this value. Setting logScanBatchSize to a lower value can help to improve the SQL performance but it will cause latency problems in the long run. If you don't have the parameter enabled then it will use the default value of 50K. Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SQL Server Source: Rebuild Index Best Practices and Recommendations
articles.description: This article covers a set of Best Practices and Recommendations when rebuilding the index of an SQL Server source. Index: Background Recommended Process Background Always stop the Qlik Replicate tasks during the index rebuild.
articles.text: This article covers a set of Best Practices and Recommendations when rebuilding the index of an SQL Server source. Index: Background Recommended Process Background Always stop the Qlik Replicate tasks during the index rebuild. This is recommended due to the following: Qlik Replicate’s reading from the active log may conflict with the rebuild index process a nd can lead to the replicate session locking the rebuild index process and then the rebuild index. The process may cause a lock to other processes running in SQL Server, including major production processes that may be locked from updating the data on SQL Server database. The rebuild index process itself can put a lock on system tables such as system_internals_partitions and thus locking the Replicate CDC process from reading changes, even on tables that their index is not currently rebuild. This can lead to various errors in replicate CDC replication. CDC reading of changes if the task is running can be slower than reading the task is down, especially when reading backup logs. Every new rebuild index operation might cause the CDC query to stop and re-run as the CDC query is filtering the changes by partition id, and each rebuild index operation might change the partition id, and so the query has to be changed. Re-running the query again can take a long time on backup logs , as it means re-reading the backup log from start ,even if CDC was already in the middle of it. Reading from the active log is usually much faster than reading from backup logs, although the different can vary in different environment, but usually reading from active is much faster. Another recommendation is to not run log backups at all during rebuild index, so Qlik Replicate will be able to read the changes from the active log. t, but usually reading from active is much faster. Another recommendation is to not run log backups at all during rebuild index, so Qlik Replicate will be able to read the changes from the active log. Since the volume of changes during rebuild index is huge, the difference in time between reading from active and backup can be significant. Another option is to not stop log backup but do stop MS Replication during rebuild index so the Tlog will be backed up but not truncated, and resume MS replication after Qlik Replicate finishes consuming the changes from active log. This method also requires Qlik Replicate to be set the “ Change processing mode (read changes from) ”. To achieve this: Open the SQL server source endpoint setting Go to the Advanced tab Locate online log and make the required change Recommended Process Stop replicate task before rebuild index Stop transaction log backup process before rebuild index Or stop MS-Replication process Run rebuild index process Once rebuild index done, let replicate consume all the changes Once Qlik Replicate caught up with all the change and source latency is low, r esume log backup (or MS-replication process) If the recommend process is not possible: Log backups can be taken, but we recommend frequent backups rather than singular large ones. It is recommended to set “ Change processing mode (read changes from) ” field in SQL server source endpoint. If the task cannot be stopped during rebuild index, you may experience the issues mentioned in item (1).

articles.title: Qlik Replicate SQL view replication: float data column inconsistency
articles.description: Data inconsistencies can be observed when replicating an SQL view from SQL to Hadoop. The column in the underlying table is of the FLOAT data type. Example: The source has 5 decimals, while the target has more than 10 .
articles.text: Data inconsistencies can be observed when replicating an SQL view from SQL to Hadoop. The column in the underlying table is of the FLOAT data type. Example: The source has 5 decimals, while the target has more than 10 . SQL Source value of the float datatype = 11.14008 T Hadoop Target value of the float datatype = 11.1400800000000001 Environment Qlik Replicate 2023.11 and later releases Resolution Qlik Replicate does not add precision explicitly. The behavior is caused by the nature of the FLOAT datatype; no configuration steps or workarounds exist to change the datatype's behavior. Cause FLOAT is, by definition, not a precise data type. For additional reading on FLOAT , see, for example: Why Floating-Point Numbers May Lose Precision (learn.microsoft.com) Precision and accuracy in floating-point calculations Internal Investigation ID(s) RECOB-8880

articles.title: Qlik Replicate stops writing to Snowflake Target
articles.description: Qlik Replicate stops sending data to a Snowflake Target reading from Log Stream Source running on a Windows OS environment. Resolution Verify that the Qlik Replicate server has a correct Proxy set up for connecting to the Snowflake Target .
articles.text: Qlik Replicate stops sending data to a Snowflake Target reading from Log Stream Source running on a Windows OS environment. Resolution Verify that the Qlik Replicate server has a correct Proxy set up for connecting to the Snowflake Target . Steps: On the Windows machine, open the ( a ) Advanced System Properties and open ( b ) Environment Variables... In the ( a ) System variables section, click ( b ) New... Create a new variable as follows: Variable name : http_proxy Variable value : http://my.proxyserver.com:8080 (this depends on your environment) And click OK Restart the Replicate Windows Server Cause The connectivity to the Snowflake Target does connect via proxy at times depending on the workload to the Snowflake Target and without the environment variables being set this causes the connection to stall and stop sending .CSV files to the Target. Related Content https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/odbc/odbc-parameters Environment Qlik Replicate
