articles.description: Qlik Replicate does support communication encryption between Replicate Server and Teradata Server, however it's disabled by default. Below steps show how to enable it.
articles.text: Qlik Replicate does support communication encryption between Replicate Server and Teradata Server, however it's disabled by default. Below steps show how to enable it. Environment All Qlik Replicate versions All supported Teradata ODBC Drivers Steps In Teradata target endpoint, open "Advanced" tab and add Internal Parameters "td_data_encryption" , set its value to ON (default is OFF): Related Content After the encryption enabled, below information can be found (below sample lines are based on Replicate 2021.5 and Teradata Driver 17.10). in Task log file: 2021-12-13T16:13:11:758929 [TARGET_LOAD ]T: conn->AddAttribute(TD_DATA_ENCRYPTION,ON) (teradata_tpt_engine.cpp:1105) in Teradata trace log file (if the trace log is enabled): 12/13/2021 16:13:11:775 PC_GETATTRIBUTE: attribute: 'DataEncryption' ... ... 12/13/2021 16:13:11:775 PC_GETCLIATTRS: DataEncryption: 'ON' Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Replicate - How to solve Teradata target error 224 Type: CLIv2_error_type(2) Message: EM_NOHOST: no DBC found in hosts file. Name not in host file
articles.description: While using the Teradata as the target database, sometimes we get the below error: [TARGET_LOAD ]E: TPT execution error: Phase: Initiate Status: 224 Type: CLIv2_error_type (2) Message: EM_NOHOST: no DBC found in hosts file. Name not in host file .
articles.text: While using the Teradata as the target database, sometimes we get the below error: [TARGET_LOAD ]E: TPT execution error: Phase: Initiate Status: 224 Type: CLIv2_error_type (2) Message: EM_NOHOST: no DBC found in hosts file. Name not in host file . [1020422] [TARGET_LOAD ]E: AR_TD_User_Action_224: TPT operator failed in resolving connection parameters. Connection details are held at the system HOSTS file. Action: Locate this file and add an entry for mapping the connection. First column would identify the server IP address. Second column stands for the host name. Next, your Teradata database should be specified followed by COP1. Example: 190.171.159.12 190.171.159.12 MYDBcop1 # My example [1020422] This is because of BTEQ, TTU and other Teradata native CLI clients expect the host names of the Teradata server nodes to be composed of the tdpid (which identifies the Teradata system) concatenated with the suffix "cop1", "cop2", etc., which identifies a specific node. To solve the problem, add line in the "hosts" file of the Replicate server (Windows, and/or Linux), for example: 190.171.159.12 MYDBcop1 where "190.171.159.12" is the Teradata Server IP Address, and "MYDB" is the target database name. "cop1"/"cop2"... is the fixed suffix. Reference link: Teradata docs Environment All Supported Qlik Replicate versions All Supported Teradata Client/Server versions (exception: v17.10) Internal Investigation ID(s): Support cases: 00036411/00033530/00032051/00026146

articles.title: Replicate - How to store before-image data in target table
articles.description: Sometimes we need to store column's before-image data in the target table. This is useful if we want to store both of the before-image and after-image of the columns values in the target table for downstream apps usage.
articles.text: Sometimes we need to store column's before-image data in the target table. This is useful if we want to store both of the before-image and after-image of the columns values in the target table for downstream apps usage. Environment Qlik Replicate All supported versions Detailed Steps: Under Apply Changes mode (Store changes mode is turn off), in the table setting by adding a new column in transformation (name it as "prevenient_salary" in this sample), the variable expression is like $BI__ < columnName > where $BI__ is a mandatory prefix (which instructs Replicate to capture the before-image data) and < columnName > is the original table column. For example if the original table column name is SALARY then $BI__ SALARY is the column before-image data: If the column SALARY value is updated from 22 to 33 in source side, then before the UPDATE the target table row looks like: after the UPDATE is applied to target table the row looks like: In this sample the before-image value is 22, the after-image value is 33. Related Content before-image data can be used in filer also, see sample here . Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Replicate - MySQL source defect and fix (2022.5 & 2022.11)
articles.description: Replicate reported errors during resume task if source MySQL running on Windows (while MySQL running on Linux then no problem) [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]I: Stream positioning at context '$.000034:3506:-1:3506:0' [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]T: Read next binary log event failed;…
articles.text: Replicate reported errors during resume task if source MySQL running on Windows (while MySQL running on Linux then no problem) [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]I: Stream positioning at context '$.000034:3506:-1:3506:0' [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]T: Read next binary log event failed; mariadb_rpl_fetch error 1236 (Could not find first log file name in binary log index file) Replicate reported errors at MySQL source endpoints sometimes (does not matter what's the MySQL source platforms): [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]W: The given Source Change Position points inside a transaction. Replicate will ignore this transaction and will capture events from the next BEGIN or DDL events. Environment: Replicate 2022.5 PR4 (2022.5.0.815) Replicate 2022.11 PR1 (2022.11.0.289) MySQL source database , any version Fix Version & Resolution: Upgrade to Replicate 2022.11 PR2 (2022.11.0.394, released already) or higher, or Replicate 2022.5 PR5 (coming soon) Workaround: If you are running 2022.5 PR3 (or lower), then keep run it, or upgrade to PR5 (or higher) . No workaround for 2022.11 (GA, or PR01) . Cause & Internal Investigation ID(s): Jira: RECOB-6526 , Description: It would not be possible to resume a task if MySQL Server was on Windows Jira: RECOB-6499 , Description: Resuming a task from a CTI event, would sometimes result in missing events or/and a redundant warning message Related Content: support case #00066196 support case #00063985 (# 00049357 ) Qlik Replicate - MySQL source defect and fix (2023.11) Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Replicate - SAP Hana source : General error 129 Search result size limit exceeded
articles.description: Replicate Error for SAP Hana source endpoint : [SOURCE_UNLOAD ]E: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: S1000 NativeError: 129 Message: [SAP AG][LIBODBCHDB DLL][HDBODBC]General error;129 transaction rolled back by an internal error: Search result size limit exceeded:…
articles.text: Replicate Error for SAP Hana source endpoint : [SOURCE_UNLOAD ]E: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: S1000 NativeError: 129 Message: [SAP AG][LIBODBCHDB DLL][HDBODBC]General error;129 transaction rolled back by an internal error: Search result size limit exceeded: 2254282483 [1022502] (ar_odbc_stmt.c:2789) Cause There is a limitation in SAP HANA , on the number of the records. In very specific scenarios limits for (intermediate) result sets exist, e.g. 2147483648 (2 billion). If the source table total rows number exceeds the 2 billion limitation , Replicate reports above error (in this sample, the user table total row number is 2254282483 ). Resolution Because the table is too big to do Full Load by a single retrieve query from source SAP Hana, we need to split the single source table read return set to multiple return sets. There are several options: 1. In a single task, Parallel Load helps if both source and target endpoints are in supported list; however if target is not in parallel load support list, eg for Kafka target, we need to break down the table into multiple tasks by using filter, and "passthru filter" should be used (passthru filter take actions on Full Load only, CDC will not be affected). see below options 2 and 3. 2. If part of the data (aka history data rows) will not being updated during the load Let's say the table will be divided into 2 tasks. Each task loads part of records. (1). Create following tasks TASK1: Full Load Only with passthru filter on PK which are history data rows, or a history rows partition TASK2: Full Load + CDC with passthru filter on PK which maybe being updated (2). Start TASK1 first, after it's done, and then start TASK2 3. Sometimes it's impossible to know if a row will be updated or not, or any row maybe being updated, then option 2 does not work. We may use this method. Let's say the table will be divided into 3 tasks. Each task loads 1M records. know if a row will be updated or not, or any row maybe being updated, then option 2 does not work. We may use this method. Let's say the table will be divided into 3 tasks. Each task loads 1M records. (1). Create following tasks TASK1: Full Load Only with passthru filter on PK (1...1,000,000) TASK2: Full Load Only with passthru filter on PK (1,000,001 ... 2,000,000) TASK3: Full Load + CDC with passthru filter on PK (2,000,001 ... 3,000,000) (2). In the TASK3, change the Full Load settings as below: Enable the "Before cached changes have been applied" option box (3). Start TASK3 first, and then start other tasks. (4). Once Full Load processes are completed for all tasks, resume TASK3 for CDC. Environment SAP Hana as source endpoint for Qlik Replicate All supported Replicate versions Related Content Internal support case ID: # 00043314. Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Replicate 2022.5.0.291 using incorrect default values for Snowflake timeout parameters
articles.description: After customers upgraded to the initial version of Replicate 2022.5 they encountered query timeout errors like: Error forwarding bulk Failed to apply UPDATE (3) for table 22 Failed to execute bulk update statement.
articles.text: After customers upgraded to the initial version of Replicate 2022.5 they encountered query timeout errors like: Error forwarding bulk Failed to apply UPDATE (3) for table 22 Failed to execute bulk update statement. RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: HY000 NativeError: 15 Message: [Snowflake][Snowflake] (15) Query has timed out. User specified timeout in seconds=60, Elapsed=90 Adjusting internal parameters or ODBC parameters were not changing the behavior. Resolution This issue is fixed in 2022.5 sp01. Please contact Support if you need access to 2022.5 SP01. The fix addressed an issue with incorrect default values being assigned to internal parameters. For the Snowflake target, it was loadTimeout and executeTimeout getting the wrong values and they were unable to be adjusted manually via internal parameters. Sp01 fixes the incorrect internal parameter defaults and allows you to adjust if needed. If you needed to increase the query timeout values, you go to: Manage endpoint connection Snowflake target Advanced tab Internal parameters: executeTimeout : 180 loadTimeout : 1800 Information provided on this defect is given as is at the time of documenting. For up to date information, please review the most recent Release Notes, or contact support with the ID 2022.5 sp01 for reference. Fix Version: 2022.5 sp01 Cause Product Defect ID: RECOB-5493 Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Replicate error for DB2LUW - SQL0628N with multiple or conflicting keywords
articles.description: The Task is targeting DB2LUW and is erroring out with the following messages. The problem can occur for both Full Load and CDC: Full Load: [TARGET_LOAD ]V: Execute immediate: 'ALTER TABLE "SCHEMA"."TABLENAME" activate not logged initially with empty table'…
articles.text: The Task is targeting DB2LUW and is erroring out with the following messages. The problem can occur for both Full Load and CDC: Full Load: [TARGET_LOAD ]V: Execute immediate: 'ALTER TABLE "SCHEMA"."TABLENAME" activate not logged initially with empty table' (ar_odbc_stmt.c:4279) ... [TARGET_LOAD ]T: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 42613 NativeError: -628 Message: [IBM][CLI Driver][DB2/LINUXX8664] SQL0628N Multiple or conflicting keywords involving the "ACTIVATE NOT LOGGED INITIALLY" clause are present. SQLSTATE=42613 [1022502] (ar_odbc_stmt.c:4356) CDC: [TARGET_APPLY ]E: RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 42613 NativeError: -628 Message: [IBM][CLI Driver][DB2/LINUXX8664] SQL0628N Multiple or conflicting keywords involving the "ACTIVATE NOT LOGGED INITIALLY" clause are present. SQLSTATE=42613 [1022502] (ar_odbc_stmt.c:4356) ... [TARGET_APPLY ]E: Failed to truncate net changes table [1022502] (odbc_bulk.c:627) Other related errors: ERROR [55019] [IBM][DB2/LINUXX8664] SQL20054N The table "lob options prohibited with blocknonlogged enabled" is in an invalid state for the operation. Reason code="". Cause: The problem is caused by a system parameter on the DB2LUW called BLOCKNONLOGGED being set to YES. The reason for setting this parameter could be any of the followings: Security This requires 100% audibility of the database, no unlogged activity is allowed. HADR environments Do not want to allow LOB columns being made with the NOT LOGGED parameter, as when the activity is switched to the standby database, risk of losing data exists. Avoid users from doing a LOAD NONRECOVERABLE or LOAD COPY NO, because after such a load the tables are also no longer in sync on the standby database. Problem Resolution: The solution is to disable this parameter by setting BLOCKNONLOGGED to NO. Please, note that this is the default setting for DB2LUW. also no longer in sync on the standby database. Problem Resolution: The solution is to disable this parameter by setting BLOCKNONLOGGED to NO. Please, note that this is the default setting for DB2LUW. If this is not possible, we can modify the DB2LUW syntax file to remove the "NOT LOGGED" keyword as follows: 1. Modify “data_type_mapping” section. Remove the highlighted sections: "data_type_mapping": [{ "rep_type": "kAR_DATA_TYPE_BLOB", "provider_data_type": "BLOB(2G) NOT LOGGED", "casting_data_type": "BLOB(2G)" }, { "rep_type": "kAR_DATA_TYPE_CLOB", "provider_data_type": "CLOB(2G) NOT LOGGED", "casting_data_type": "CLOB(2G)" }], 2. Modify "query_syntax"."truncate_table" value: "truncate_table": "TRUNCATE TABLE ${QO}${TABLE_OWNER}${QC}.${QO}${TABLE_NAME}${QC} REUSE STORAGE IGNORE DELETE TRIGGERS IMMEDIATE"​ 3. Add a specific temporary table clause to "query_syntax"."truncate_table": "create_temporary_table": "CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE ${QO}${TABLE_OWNER}${QC}.${QO}${TABLE_NAME}${QC} ( ${COLUMN_LIST} ) LOGGED ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS", Custom Syntax File: An already modified syntax file is attached to this article (DB2_MRG_LOGGED.JSON). To use this syntax file, perform the followings: Copy the Syntax file to the data/imports folder. Run the command line and import the syntax: repctl putobject data=DB2_MRG_LOGGED.JSON To use the new syntax, edit the DB2LUW Target Endpoint (ODBC), in the Advanced tab set the Provider Syntax to DB2_MRG_LOGGED.

articles.title: Replicate jobs are not running as per schedule
articles.description: Check what is the scheduler set for the task in question: In the Server setting / Scheduler verify if the task is set to use Server local time or UTC time Verify if the task is still running or if many tasks were running at the same time causing the scheduler…
articles.text: Check what is the scheduler set for the task in question: In the Server setting / Scheduler verify if the task is set to use Server local time or UTC time Verify if the task is still running or if many tasks were running at the same time causing the scheduler to be delayed. If everything looks correct on the job scheduler setting: Verify the server logs for errors or alerts Server setting / Logging: View Logs, best to download the logs and view in a text editor, like notepad++ In Notepad++ search the task name that was scheduled to run, search all in the document.

articles.title: Replicate not picking up unique index
articles.description: Unique indexes that are sorted in descending order will not be read by Qlik Replicate. The tables would be treated as though it does not have any unique indexes.
articles.text: Unique indexes that are sorted in descending order will not be read by Qlik Replicate. The tables would be treated as though it does not have any unique indexes. This can cause other issues if you do not have any primary keys or other unique indexes on the table. Environment Qlik Replicate Oracle as a source endpoint Resolution The unique index will need to be created without descending order applied to the index or another unique index will need to be created for the table. Cause When an index is created with Descending, Oracle creates the index as a function-based index. Replicate does not support function-based indexes. Limitation: Function-based indexes are not supported. Oracle as a source limitations

articles.title: Replicate Port Description
articles.description: Until Replicate 5.0 Replicate server severed requests (from the GUI/command line) based on RPC API based on Google protobuf. This RPC API is known as ‘repctl commands’.
articles.text: Until Replicate 5.0 Replicate server severed requests (from the GUI/command line) based on RPC API based on Google protobuf. This RPC API is known as ‘repctl commands’. When exposed REST API in Replicate server we actually introduce additional server (that run as a thread on the same repctl server process). The REST server (called atctl internally) is actually translate the REST request to the old RPC server that run on the same process. The RPC server used to run on port 3552. Because it was to not force open a new port in the firewall and switched the RPC server port to 3550 and allocated 3552 for the new REST server. The RPC server runs on both the Replicate server and each and every one of the Replicate task processes. The communication between the Replicate server and the Replicate tasks is done using this RPC API.

articles.title: Replicate Postgres Source Error Converting Timestamp
articles.description: [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]E: Error in converting TIMESTAMP '2020-06-08 02:43:27.336723+00' from textual representation into structured format [1022502] (postgres_endpoint_wal_utils.c:3022) Environment Qlik Replicate version 6.6 hosted on Windoww Resolution Check with…
articles.text: [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]E: Error in converting TIMESTAMP '2020-06-08 02:43:27.336723+00' from textual representation into structured format [1022502] (postgres_endpoint_wal_utils.c:3022) Environment Qlik Replicate version 6.6 hosted on Windoww Resolution Check with your Windows server admin before making the change. Open environment variables on your Replicate server. Press the windows button and type in env and you'll see an option for "Edit the System Environment Variables", click that to open it. On the System Properties window that opens, click the Environment Variables button. On the screen that opens, below the System variables section at the bottom of the screen, click new. On the screen that opens put PGDATESTYLE as the variable name and ISO as the variable value. Make sure there are no leading or trailing spaces. Click OK to save the new variable, and click OK to close the Environment Variables screen, and the System Properties window. Stop and resume the task. Check to confirm that the issue is resolved, if not, restart the Replicate services (this will stop and resume all your tasks). If the issue is still not resolved, reboot the Replicate server to ensure that the new environment variable is in effect. Related Content https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.6/libpq-envars.html

articles.title: Replicate Red Hat 8 SQL Server Source fails TCP Provider: Error code 0x2746
articles.description: Replicate 2022.5 fails to connect to SQL Server Source Endpoint when connecting from Red Had Linux 8 using the libmsodbcsql-17.10.so.1.1 or libmsodbcsql-17.6.so.1.1.
articles.text: Replicate 2022.5 fails to connect to SQL Server Source Endpoint when connecting from Red Had Linux 8 using the libmsodbcsql-17.10.so.1.1 or libmsodbcsql-17.6.so.1.1. Error: Failed to connect RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 08001 NativeError: 10054 Message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]TCP Provider: Error code 0x2746 Resolution Update the openssl.conf on the Replicate Server running on the Red Hat Linux 8 environment. information provided on this defect is given as is at the time of documenting. For up-to-date information, please review the most recent Release Notes with the ID RECOB-6147 for reference. Workaround: Go to directory /etc/pki/tls/ on the Linux Replicate Server and backup the openssl.conf file and add the below entries: You need to add this to the beginning of your config file: openssl_conf = default_conf or Change the value for openssl_conf to default_conf if the line already exists and make sure to added these entries [default_conf] ssl_conf = ssl_sect [ssl_sect] system_default = system_default_sect [system_default_sect] MinProtocol = TLSv1.2 CipherString = DEFAULT@SECLEVEL=1 Restart the Linux Server for the changes to take affect Fix Version: Replicate 2023 version Cause The error with the connection is due to the TLS 1.2 version that is the Red Hat 8 default and the Replicate environment having reference to the TLS 1.1 version. Environment Qlik Replicate 2022.5 Related Content Welcome to the Qlik Replicate online help

articles.title: Replicate Sorter Files
articles.description: Sorter files are located on the data directory of the Replicate server. Sample location: C:\Program Files\Attunity\Replicate\data\tasks\<task name>\ sorter The twsp files are transactions that have not been applied to target yet.
articles.text: Sorter files are located on the data directory of the Replicate server. Sample location: C:\Program Files\Attunity\Replicate\data\tasks\<task name>\ sorter The twsp files are transactions that have not been applied to target yet. They are automatically purged after use. Sorter files will accumulate if there if either: Big transactions from the source are not committed yet Target transactions are not applied yet Target transactions have been applied but no confirmation was returned You can not control the size of the sorter file h owever you can configure Replicate to use more memory and a longer transaction timeout. Increasing the Transaction Offload Tuning values can help, especially the Transactions duration exceeds the default values. Locate the settings in: Designer --> Task Settings --> Change Processing --> Change Processing Tuning --> Transaction Offload Tuning Total transactions memory size exceeds (MB): Set this to a larger memory allocation, such as 4G, 8G etc, depending on the total memory of the AR server. Transactions duration exceeds (seconds): Set to a longer time, eg 1 hour etc, depending on the transaction requirements. It is not advisable to delete the tswp files in the sorter file as this will impact Replicate's ability to process the changes. It acts as a landing zone for changes which have not been applied to the target, so deleting those files can cause unexpected behaviour and possibly data loss.

articles.title: Replicate Target Endpoint Teradata  Version 15 or higher  ODBC requirements
articles.description: Replicate Target Endpoint Teradata Version 15 or higher ODBC requirements Setting up Replicate to push data via Load and or CDC Process to Teradata 15 or higher you will need to install the 16.20 ODBC driver with the TPT modules which are separate components…
articles.text: Replicate Target Endpoint Teradata Version 15 or higher ODBC requirements Setting up Replicate to push data via Load and or CDC Process to Teradata 15 or higher you will need to install the 16.20 ODBC driver with the TPT modules which are separate components with the new ODBC version. Environment Windows Replicate 2021.11 2022.5 Install the Teradata Tools and Utilities Base which can be downloaded from the Teradata site: https://downloads.teradata Run the setup under the Windows\TTU folder. Make sure you install the TPT components Teradata Parallel Base and Parallel Stream. The newer ODBC driver has the TPT modules separate where as the older 15 ODBC driver the TPT is included in the ODBC layer.

articles.title: Replicate Teradata target - How to determine the ERROR-table and LOAD-table name for TPT Load tables especially for long name tables
articles.description: How to determine the ERROR-table and LOAD-table name for TPT Load tables especially for long name tables? When Replicate uses TPT Load to do FullLoad , Replicate specify TPT Load's ErrorTable naming rule is like: "TABLE_NAME(The first 14 chars)_NNNNNNNNN(12…
articles.text: How to determine the ERROR-table and LOAD-table name for TPT Load tables especially for long name tables? When Replicate uses TPT Load to do FullLoad , Replicate specify TPT Load's ErrorTable naming rule is like: "TABLE_NAME(The first 14 chars)_NNNNNNNNN(12 chars unique number)_E0" "TABLE_NAME(The first 14 chars)_NNNNNNNNN(12 chars unique number)_E1" the whole error-table name length is 30 characters. However if the original source tables name's first 14 chars are duplicate, then how can we tell the relationship between the TPD loaded table and Error-table. Environment All Supported Qlik Replicate #Version All Supported Teradata versions Detailed information For example In Oracle DB (or any source DB) there are 2 tables which name is similar (whole length is 22, the first 14 chars are duplicate): VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_A VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_B In Full Load Replicate composes unique error-tables for them: 2022-03-04T19:55:18 [TARGET_LOAD ]I: TD_LOAD error tables for LOAD phase are: "targetdb"."VERYLOOOOOOOOO_0000F40E0000_E1" , "targetdb"."VERYLOOOOOOOOO_0000F40E0000_E2" 2022-03-04T19:55:18 [TARGET_LOAD ]I: TD_LOAD error tables for LOAD phase are: "targetdb"."VERYLOOOOOOOOO_0000F50E0000_E1" , "targetdb"."VERYLOOOOOOOOO_0000F50E0000_E2" In Teradata each table is identified by a unique hexadecimal value called the TVMID (or called TABLEID). Replicate uses it to identify the error-table. It's easy to get the TVMID by query (test by Teradata 17.10): select TVMName,TVMId from DBC.TVM where TVMName='VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_A'; VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_A 00-00-f4-0e-00-00​ select TVMName,TVMId from DBC.TVM where TVMName='VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_B'; VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_B 00-00-f5-0e-00-00​ (Note the TVMID changes if the table was dropped/recreated). 20_A 00-00-f4-0e-00-00​ select TVMName,TVMId from DBC.TVM where TVMName='VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_B'; VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_B 00-00-f5-0e-00-00​ (Note the TVMID changes if the table was dropped/recreated). That's the relationship between the source table and error-table: VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_A error table name is VERYLOOOOOOOOO_0000 F4 0E0000_E1 VERYLOOOOOOOOOOONG20_B error table name is VERYLOOOOOOOOO_0000 F5 0E0000_E1 Related Content Support case: #00025521 FR request We can't judge error table name

articles.title: Replicate using Oracle source fails with missing redo log
articles.description: Environment Qlik Replicate If a Replicate task fails with the following error: 00008696: 2021-01-20T10:06:02:964052 [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]E: Cannot find archived REDO log with sequence '7204', thread '1' (oracdc_reader.c:412) OR 00005624:…
articles.text: Environment Qlik Replicate If a Replicate task fails with the following error: 00008696: 2021-01-20T10:06:02:964052 [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]E: Cannot find archived REDO log with sequence '7204', thread '1' (oracdc_reader.c:412) OR 00005624: 2020-06-02T17:05:23:665747 [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]E: Oracle CDC stopped [1022301] (oracdc_merger.c:1178) Replicate is always reading V$archived_log to get the archived REDO information. The redo log needs to have an active/available status from the V$archived_log Cause This means that Replicate is complaining that it cannot find the redo archive file. Either 1. the Replicate Oracle Source Endpoint should be using a different Oracle DEST_ID; 2. the file does not exist on disk; or 3. the file exists but that the internal Oracle metadata in v$archived_log view says that it's not available. The simplest explanation is that the redo log could just have been deleted before Replicate was able to process it. Resolution We recommend to at least keep it for 72 hours in case of unexpected weekend issues. What you can do as well if you encounter an issue like this, is to restore the oracle redo log and then resume the task. If the redo log cannot be restored, then you need to reload the entire task.

articles.title: Replicate-DB2z SSL Configuration
articles.description: Abstract: This knowledge base article takes a look at the client side setup for SSL connections from the Qlik Replicate server to a DB2/Z source endpoint.
articles.text: Abstract: This knowledge base article takes a look at the client side setup for SSL connections from the Qlik Replicate server to a DB2/Z source endpoint. It assumes that that DB2 on z/OS (the server side) has already been set up according to IBM documentation and is listening for incoming secure connections. It also assumes that the network connections (routers and firewalls) between the mainframe and the Replicate server have been configured to support the necessary socket ports and protocols. Prerequisites: The following software packages need to be installed on the Replicate Server in order for the endpoint (client) to complete a secure connection to DB2 for z/OS: - DB2 CLI / ODBC V11.1 Driver or above from IBM (ex: v11.1.4fp4a_ntx64_odbc_cli.zip) - GSKit 8 or above from IBM (ex: 8.0.55.4-ISS-GSKIT-WinX64-FP004.zip) – note that some DB2 client driver kits come with a subset of GSK, making this prereq optional. x: v11.1.4fp4a_ntx64_odbc_cli.zip) - GSKit 8 or above from IBM (ex: 8.0.55.4-ISS-GSKIT-WinX64-FP004.zip) – note that some DB2 client driver kits come with a subset of GSK, making this prereq optional. Configuring the Client: One or more of the following steps may be required, depending on platform and approach to DB2 DSN setup: Db2dsdriver.cfg – in this example we are creating a DSN named DB2T (enter your own ip address and port) <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no" ?> <configuration> <dsncollection> <dsn alias="DB2T" host="<ipaddress>" name="DSNDB2T" port="<port>"> <parameter name="SecurityTransportMode" value="SSL"/> <parameter name="SSLClientKeystoredb" value="c:\temp\keystore.kdb"/> <parameter name="SSLClientKeystash" value="c:\temp\keystore.sth"/> </dsn> </dsncollection> <databases> <database host="<ipaddress>" name="DSNDB2T" port="<port>"> <wlb> <parameter name="enableWLB" value="false"/> </wlb> <acr> <parameter name="enableACR" value="true"/> </acr> </database> </databases> </configuration> Create the ODBC DSN (windows screenshots, linux also has wizards if desktop is installed, or manual setup of odbc.ini and odbcinst.ini: Select IBM DB2 ODBC DRIVER and then Finish Insert the Database Name in the Data source name Field and then OK Open the just created System DSN, change to Advanced Settings and remove the DBAlias Entry. Create a keystore and add a certificate gsk8capicmd -keydb -create -db c:\temp\keystore.kdb -pw ser123 -stash Add a root certificate gsk8capicmd -cert -create -db c:\temp\keystore.kdb -pw serv123 -label "SERVCA1" -dn "CN=SERVCA1" Verify the keystore gsk8capicmd -cert -list -db c:\temp\keystore.kdb -pw serv123 Certificates found * default, - personal, ! eate -db c:\temp\keystore.kdb -pw serv123 -label "SERVCA1" -dn "CN=SERVCA1" Verify the keystore gsk8capicmd -cert -list -db c:\temp\keystore.kdb -pw serv123 Certificates found * default, - personal, ! trusted, # secret key - SERVCA1 If using GSK_MS_CERTIFICATE_STORE (Windows Only) Extract root certificate: gsk8capicmd -cert -extract -db c:\temp\keystore.kdb -pw serv123 -label " SERVCA1 " -target c:\temp\ temp1.arm Add to the MS CERTIFICATE STORE gsk8capicmd -cert -add -db GSK_MS_CERTIFICATE_STORE -label "SERVCA1" -file c:\temp\temp1.arm Make reference to the MS CERTIFICATE STORE in the db2dsdriver.cfg configuration: <parameter name="SSLClientKeystoredb" value="GSK_MS_CERTIFICATE_STORE"/> Configure the Endpoint Internal Parameters (Advanced Tab) additionalConnectionProperties: Security=SSL SSLClientKeystoredb=GSK_MS_CERTIFICATE_STORE (or actual kdb file) CURSORHOLD=1 DESCRIBEPARAM=1 CONCURRENTACCESSRESOLUTION=1 More Information: Additional information can be found at the following links: GSK User Guide: ftp://ftp.software.ibm.com/software/webserver/appserv/library/v80/GSK_CapiCmd_UserGuide.pdf Example use case: https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSYQBZ_9.6.0/com.ibm.doors.configuring.doc/topics/r_e...

articles.title: Replicating and Transforming Semi-structured Data with Replicate and Compose
articles.description: This whitepaper discusses how to convert and consume semi-structured data with the Qlik Data Integration solution. Today, most on-line transactional processing systems (OLTP) store data in a tabular format of tables and columns.
articles.text: This whitepaper discusses how to convert and consume semi-structured data with the Qlik Data Integration solution. Today, most on-line transactional processing systems (OLTP) store data in a tabular format of tables and columns. In most cases, data is stored in SQL databases such as Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Oracle,Snowflake and others, that support a variety of data types such as character, datetime, numeric, varchar, and more. Additionally, support for new data types such as Character Large Object (CLOB), Geography (GEO), JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) and Extensible Markup Language (XML) were added as databases evolved. This whitepaper shows how to replicate and transform semi-structured data with Qlik Replicate and Qlik Compose for Data Warehouses. The examples covered in this article are based on the semi-structured data format called JavaScript Object Notation (JSON).

articles.title: Replicating tables to Kafka with column names containing forward slashes
articles.description: SAP and other database applications may include tables with column names that include forward slashes. These can cause unexpected (and unwanted) results when replicating to Kafka.
articles.text: SAP and other database applications may include tables with column names that include forward slashes. These can cause unexpected (and unwanted) results when replicating to Kafka. Resolution: Many databases support the use of forward slashes as part of a column name. Applications such as SAP commonly utilize them. The following simple table defined in DB2 LUW will serve as the example for this scenario: db2 => create table kafkatest (col1 int, "/COL2" int, "/COL/C3" int, col4 int) db2 => insert into kafkatest values(1,1,1,1) db2 => insert into kafkatest values(2,2,2,2) Without any special attention being paid to the columns with forward slashes, Qlik Replication will accept the “kafkatest” table as a valid source table and will replicate the data to Kafka. The resulting JSON messages sent to Kafla will be formatted like this example: { "magic": "atMSG", "type": "DT", "headers": null, "messageSchemaId": null, "messageSchema": null, "message": { "data": { "COL1": 1, "COL4": 1 }, "COL2": 1, "COL": { "C3": 1 }, "beforeData": null, "headers": { "operation": "REFRESH", "changeSequence": "", "timestamp": "", "streamPosition": "", "transactionId": "", "changeMask": null, "columnMask": null } } Notice: The COL1 and COL4 (in blue) can be found within the “data” object. /COL2 and /COL/C3 (in red) are part of the Kafka message but are outside of the “data” object. Using a Task Global Transformation: Replication tasks often contain many tables in a single task, some or all of which could include one or more columns with forward slashes. The forward slashes, wherever they are in use, can convert using a single task Global Transformation. This can be defined through the Designer UI as shown here: 1: Open Global Transformations for the current task. 2: Create a new Global Transformation. 3: Select Rename column as the type of transformation. can be defined through the Designer UI as shown here: 1: Open Global Transformations for the current task. 2: Create a new Global Transformation. 3: Select Rename column as the type of transformation. 4: Indicate which tables and columns are in scope for the transformation. 5: Define a transformation expression. 6: Use the “replace” function to replace forward slashes with the desired character (or characters). In the example the forward slash replaces an underscore. 7: Test the expression and then click OK to accept it. 8: Proceed with the Global Transformation definition. 9: Finish the Global Transformation then save changes to the task (not shown). The resulting JSON output to Kafka with the Global Transformation from the sample table will look like this: { "magic": "atMSG", "type": "DT", "headers": null, "messageSchemaId": null, "messageSchema": null, "message": { "data": { "COL1": 1, "_COL2": 1, "_COL_C3": 1, "COL4": 1 }, "beforeData": null, "headers": { "operation": "REFRESH", "changeSequence": "", "timestamp": "", "streamPosition": "", "transactionId": "", "changeMask": null, "columnMask": null } } } The columns with forward slashes now contain underscores and all of the columns are now accounted for within the “data” object (in blue).

articles.title: Replicating through Qlik Replicate to Databricks SQL Warehouse
articles.description: To successfully configure your S3 storage bucket (staging) on your SQL Warehouse, first follow the instructions outlined in Setting general connection properties (help.qlik.com).
articles.text: To successfully configure your S3 storage bucket (staging) on your SQL Warehouse, first follow the instructions outlined in Setting general connection properties (help.qlik.com). In addition: Add an instance profile or service principle (IAM user) to your Compute which has access to the S3 storage bucket. This is the same S3 bucket you enter into your Qlik Replicate endpoint for Staging. You can navigate to the Data Access properties section of your SQL Warehouse through your Workspace settings. Click on your User Name in the upper right corner => Click Settings => Compute => SQL warehouses (Manage). See: Configure a SQL warehouse to use an instance profile Connect to Amazon S3 If you choose to use Unity Catalog, you need to add an external storage location for the S3 storage bucket. Again, this is the same bucket you enter in the Replicate endpoint for staging. Unity Catalog is not technically a requirement but if you choose to utilize Serverless we recommend you use Unity instead of the Hive Metastore. See: Create a storage credential for connecting to AWS S3 Create an external location to connect cloud storage to Databricks Environment: Qlik Replicate

articles.title: Replication of MS SQL tables that include computed columns
articles.description: When running a Replicate task with MS SQL source endpoint , replication of computed columns is supported for Full Load only. This limitation is also mentioned in the Replicate User Guide: “"Replication of computed columns is supported in Full Load replication…
articles.text: When running a Replicate task with MS SQL source endpoint , replication of computed columns is supported for Full Load only. This limitation is also mentioned in the Replicate User Guide: “"Replication of computed columns is supported in Full Load replication tasks only. During change processing, INSERTs to computed columns will appear as NULL on the target and UPDATEs will be ignored ." If you have a table with computed column and you would still like that the value of the computed column will be replicated to the target you can do one of the following: Option 1 : In the Replicate UI under task design --> Table settings (of the table with the computed column) --> transform Remove the computed column from the output columns list Add a new column (with the name that you wish to be created in the target) and define the desired computation expression (should be similar to the computation expression defined for the computed column in the source endpoint) Note : with this setting Replicate will do the required computation (instead of the db). Option 2: In the target endpoint create the table DDL with the computed column expression manually In the Replicate UI under task setting --> Full Load --> Full Load Settings --> If target table already exists: set the option to ‘TRUNCATE before loading’ Note : this setting affects all task tables. i.e. if you choose this option you would have to create by yourself, in the target endpoint, the DDL of all tables included in the task. If you wish, you can set Replicate to suspend tables with computed columns that are included in CDC tasks. This can be done by setting the internal parameter suspendTableWithComputedColumn to True (under the MS SQL source endpoint à advanced tab à internal parameters)

articles.title: Repliweb Eraser using wrong domain account
articles.description: The Repliweb eraser tool is using the incorect domain account. In effect, the account may be locked out if the wrong password was associated with the account.
articles.text: The Repliweb eraser tool is using the incorect domain account. In effect, the account may be locked out if the wrong password was associated with the account. How do I update the account being used with Repliweb Eraser tool? Environment Repliweb R1 version 6.xx Resolution There could be a case, where the user uses the domain account to log in to the console and creates a scheduler job. This would have stored the domain account at that time. Solution 1 Delete the scheduler and recreate it. Solution 2 Manually delete the backup file. Go into the backup and change any available setting (example, change the minute) Save the new setting for the backup, so that the backup job run with your new credentials Solution 3 R1 caches the password for the clean up job. You can use the password change utility within the R1 Console / Manage /Center / Tools / Change password. The cleanup jobs are under the ~\rds\scheduler\active\actve_e raser\ you can see the report.log on the failure of the job and edges as well.

articles.title: Resolving Qlik Replicate Error Metadata Manager table definition cannot be found in the Source
articles.description: There are instances while working with Qlik Replicate that we tend to get busy and don't remember that the tool requires regular maintenance.
articles.text: There are instances while working with Qlik Replicate that we tend to get busy and don't remember that the tool requires regular maintenance. As per the unspecified recommendation, we should be restarting the Qlik Replicate Window service once a month to keep the tool in healthy condition. If we lag behind on the maintenance schedule then the tool starts behaving weird which tends to cause issues that shouldn't be an issue in the first place. I'll go ahead and discuss one of those issues in the article. Environment Qlik Replicate Error as per the log: Metadata Manager table definition cannot be found in the Source. Table ID: 121 [1021802] (metadatamanager.c:1957) Scenario: There is an existing task which is running fine for both Full Load and CDC and we try to add new tables to the task and it starts throwing this error. Cause: The team was lagging behind on the maintenance of the Qlik Replicate instance and due to that it could not update the internal metadata with the changes required for the new tables. Fix: In the Advance Run options for the task we have an option Metadata Only, which in turn has two more options: Recreate all tables and then stop: This will rebuild metadata for all available tables in the task. Create missing tables and then stop: This will rebuild metadata for only missing tables or the tables which are added newly to the task. In this particular scenario, we have to go with option 2 which will build the data from all newly added tasks and then stop. This will retain all statistics on the earlier existing tables (mentioning full load is carried out earlier and table load is complete) and the newly available tables will be ready for Full Load. Note: The information in this article is provided as-is and to be used at your own discretion. rried out earlier and table load is complete) and the newly available tables will be ready for Full Load. Note: The information in this article is provided as-is and to be used at your own discretion. articles.title: S3 - Access denied to bucket
articles.description: If you get this issue in Replicate with S3 a good process would be to take this outside of Replicate using the AWS CLI. Make sure to, download the CLI and install https://s3.amazonaws.com/aws-cli/AWSCLI64PY3.msi Configure the CLI with the same credentials…
articles.text: If you get this issue in Replicate with S3 a good process would be to take this outside of Replicate using the AWS CLI. Make sure to, download the CLI and install https://s3.amazonaws.com/aws-cli/AWSCLI64PY3.msi Configure the CLI with the same credentials used in Replicate S3/EMR Endpoint AWS configure: Run the command that Replicate would run, but outside of Replicate, for example (There may be some text files under the folder c:\temp\) AWS s3 cp c:\temp\ s://my_bucket/folder/ --include "*.txt" Note: This is just an example copying the file, but you can do a lot of things with the AWS client. For example, get the bucket location: aws s3api get-bucket-location --bucket MY_BUCKET Those are only two examples - for more options for the AWS CLI S3, feel free to use the link below: https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/documentation/api/latest/reference/s3/index.html The information in this article is provided as-is and to be used at own discretion. Depending on tool(s) used, customization(s), and/or other factors ongoing support on the solution below may not be provided by Qlik Support.

articles.title: Safely migrating existing Qlik Replicate tasks
articles.description: To safely export and import an existing Qlik Replicate task: 1. Stop the task. 2. Export the task using the Qlik Replicate Console . See Exporting tasks . 3. Import the task into the new Qlik Replicate system using the Qlik Replicate Console .
articles.text: To safely export and import an existing Qlik Replicate task: 1. Stop the task. 2. Export the task using the Qlik Replicate Console . See Exporting tasks . 3. Import the task into the new Qlik Replicate system using the Qlik Replicate Console . See Importing tasks . 4. Test the endpoints. It may be necessary to re-enter password(s). To restart with the last row processed: Look at the end of the task log from the stopped task for the Final saved task state message, for example: 00006952: 2022-05-04T18:59:51:411012 [SORTER ]I: Final saved task state. Stream position 0:1:1:1, Source id 138, next Target id 13, confirmed Target id 9, last source timestamp 1651690784747736 (sorter.c:770) Take the stream position value and add V1: in front of it. For example V1:0:1:1:1 This is the value you can use in the advanced run Source Change Position . Note that it will start with the last row that was processed. Environment Qlik Replicate

articles.title: SalesForce columns with data type of 'Picklist (Multi-Select)' are replicated to target endpoint as NULL
articles.description: When working with SalesForce source endpoint you may face a problem where columns with data type of 'Picklist (Multi-Select)' are replicated to target endpoint as NULL Cause This problem is usually caused since LOB support is disabled in task setting.
articles.text: When working with SalesForce source endpoint you may face a problem where columns with data type of 'Picklist (Multi-Select)' are replicated to target endpoint as NULL Cause This problem is usually caused since LOB support is disabled in task setting. Resolution To solve the problem you should enable LOB support in the task settings. To enable LOB support: open Task settings-->Metadata-->Target metadata, and check the box for "Replicate LOB columns" choose a LOB size limit that matches the biggest LOB in the task tables. Environment Replicate with SalesForce source endpoint

articles.title: Salesforce endpoint - Salesforce standard objects best practice
articles.description: When working with Salesforce endpoint, Replicate performs CDC using the Salesforce CDC API and is therefore subjects to its limitations. Salesforce CDC does not support all of the Salesforce standard objects.
articles.text: When working with Salesforce endpoint, Replicate performs CDC using the Salesforce CDC API and is therefore subjects to its limitations. Salesforce CDC does not support all of the Salesforce standard objects. In the link below you can find a list of the supported Salesforce CDC objects: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.change_data_capture.meta/change_data_capture/cdc_o... Objects that are not supported by Salesforce CDC API can still be replicate d in a Full Load task. It is recommended to replicate them once a day (or based on requirements), during a time window with low activity. FYI - below is a sample list of salsforce objects that are not supported by Salesforce CDC API : Event OpportunityLineItem Organisation PricebookEntry RecordType SocialPersona

articles.title: SAP -- What is the difference between SAP Application and SAP Application (DB) Endpoints?
articles.description: Tech-note - FAQ Question What is the difference between SAP Application and SAP Application (DB) Endpoints? Answer There are several architectural differences between the two endpoints.
articles.text: Tech-note - FAQ Question What is the difference between SAP Application and SAP Application (DB) Endpoints? Answer There are several architectural differences between the two endpoints. The SAPAppDB is more modern and is able to provide a great performance benefit. The DB Endpoint is also able to process pooled and clustered tables without the need for RFC calls. SAP Application Endpoint Replicate calls the custom RFC functions, provided by GoldClient. These functions provide SAP table metadata, table content for the followings: Pooled tables Cluster tables STXL table. SAP Application DB Endpoint The SAPAppDB does not need to connect to the SAP Application Server, thus the Endpoint does not require this info. All of the followings are retrieved from the underlying database: SAP Metadata. Table content.

articles.title: SAP Cluster Tables load is missing large amount of data after Replicate version upgrade
articles.description: Problem Description When upgrading to a new version of Replicate. The Full Load of the SAP Application Cluster Tables resulted in a very low data count. Comparing the data counts with the previous version of Replicate results in an accurate data counts.
articles.text: Problem Description When upgrading to a new version of Replicate. The Full Load of the SAP Application Cluster Tables resulted in a very low data count. Comparing the data counts with the previous version of Replicate results in an accurate data counts. The Task connects to the same SAP hostname on both Replicate versions. Problem Resolution Replicate requires the same major/minor version of the R4SAP. A lower version of the R4SAP could cause unpredictable behavior. To learn about the current version of the transports, you need to invoke the /nr4sap and click on About/About Replicate (SAP). The result is a listing of the last four updates, for example: To give an example of these updates, please review the following list of the transports and their build numbers: 5.5 6.0 6.1 InstallCode K901773 K902124 K902124 InstallCodeECC K901271 K901271 K901271 The list shows that Replicate v6.0 and 6.1 include the same version levels of the transports, meaning they are both compatible. One however, for example cannot install Replicate 6.1 and use the 5.5 transports. In this case make sure to upgrade to the latest transports. Upgrading the R4SAP to the same version level of Replicate resolves the issue.

articles.title: SAP Extractor missing from Source Endpoints
articles.description: There is a new Source Endpoint you are trying to create the Source Endpoint in Replicate but the SAP Extractor is not showing up in the list. The below steps should be followed to get the SAP Extractor listed as a valid Source Endpoint.
articles.text: There is a new Source Endpoint you are trying to create the Source Endpoint in Replicate but the SAP Extractor is not showing up in the list. The below steps should be followed to get the SAP Extractor listed as a valid Source Endpoint. Stop the Replicate Server (service) Copy the 2 files Sapjco3.jar and Sapjco3.dll to the {REPLICATE_INSTALL_DIR}\endpoint_srv\externals For Linux the Sapjco3.jar and libsapjco3.so files copy to the /REPLICATE_INSTALL_DIR/endpoint_srv/externals Start the Replicate Server (service) Create new Endpoint Source SAP Extractor Note: If the Source does not show up you may not have proper license for this Source Endpoint. Environment Qlik Replicate 2021.5 Qlik Replicate 2021.11 The information in this article is provided as-is and to be used at own discretion. Depending on tool(s) used, customization(s), and/or other factors ongoing support on the solution below may not be provided by Qlik Support.

articles.title: SAP Hana filter limitation on DELETE
articles.description: In the Replicate User Guide, it states: when using Log-Based CDC method, delete and updated operations are not supported for filtered records for SAP HANA source endpoint.
articles.text: In the Replicate User Guide, it states: when using Log-Based CDC method, delete and updated operations are not supported for filtered records for SAP HANA source endpoint. Ref: https://help.qlik.com/en-US/replicate/May2021/Content/Replicate/Main/SAP%20Hana%20Source/limitations... When Replicate reads a DELETE operation for SAP HANA source, it only gets the values of the columns of the PK and not any values of other columns. Thus, the limitation on DELETE is only for columns that are not part of the primary key.

articles.title: SAP HANA Source Transaction Consistency
articles.description: Environment Qlik Replicate SAP HANA source If you see this warning: [ASSERTION ]W: Some changes were either rolled back or not committed within the 60 seconds allocated for transactional consistency, and will therefore not be applied to the target…
articles.text: Environment Qlik Replicate SAP HANA source If you see this warning: [ASSERTION ]W: Some changes were either rolled back or not committed within the 60 seconds allocated for transactional consistency, and will therefore not be applied to the target (saphana_endpoint_capture_trigger_based.c:437) With SAP Hana sources we have a limitation of only supporting the longest supported transaction length of 60 seconds (by default). This is noted in the user guide. If you have transactions in your environment that exceed 60 seconds, you should set the transactional consistency to the expected transaction duration. If your transactions are longer than what is configured on the source endpoint, then t his may result in data inconsistency - possible data loss, mismatch, duplicates. Please note that if you raise it enough you may always be surprised by a long-running transaction and not mention the great added latency.

articles.title: SAP HANA Trigger based Source Endpoint General error;2055 maximum number of rows per table or partition reached
articles.description: Qlik Replicate with SAP HANA Source fails to execute copy changes script with error: Failed to execute 'Insert from cdc_changes to cdc_log table' statement RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: S1000 NativeError: 2055 Message: [SAP AG][LIBODBCHDB DLL][HDBODBC] General…
articles.text: Qlik Replicate with SAP HANA Source fails to execute copy changes script with error: Failed to execute 'Insert from cdc_changes to cdc_log table' statement RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: S1000 NativeError: 2055 Message: [SAP AG][LIBODBCHDB DLL][HDBODBC] General error;2055 maximum number of rows per table or partition reached Environment Qlik Replicate 2021.5 Qlik Replicate 2021.11 Qlik Replicate 2022.5 pre SP04 When you are replicating data from the SAP HANA environment Trigger Based Source Endpoint, the failure is due to the 2 Billion Max Row limit for the cdc_log Table which is used to process the data from Source to Target. This restriction has been lifted with the 2025.5 SP04 version of Qlik Replicate. Resolution This restriction of the cdc_log Table has been fixed in the 2022.5 version of Replicate with the application of the Service Pack 04 (Build 815) along with enabling the SAP HANA CTS feature. Please contact support for enabling CTS Support on the Endpoint. Cause There is currently a limit to the rows in the cdc_log Table which is 2 billion rows as this is the reason for the failure of the copy script to copy the data from the changes_log Table to the cdc_log Table to be processed to the Target. This restriction has been lifted with the application of Replicate 2022.5 SP04 version which now can use the SAP HANA CTS feature. Related Content How to RESUME Hana trigger-based CDC task

articles.title: SAPDB -- What are the required permissions working with SAP DB Endpoint?
articles.description: Tech-note - FAQ QUESTION What are the required permissions working with SAP Application DB Endpoint? ANSWER The SAPDB Endpoint requires database access to the following tables: DD02L DD03L DD02T DD03T T000 Depending on the transports you also need to grant…
articles.text: Tech-note - FAQ QUESTION What are the required permissions working with SAP Application DB Endpoint? ANSWER The SAPDB Endpoint requires database access to the following tables: DD02L DD03L DD02T DD03T T000 Depending on the transports you also need to grant permissions to the following tables: /HTG/GC_HEAD /HTG/GC_TABLES1 The newer version of the Transports require these instead: /HTG/GC4R_BUSGRP /HTG/GC4R_TABLES Example command in Oracle: GRANT SELECT ON SAPSR3./HTG/GC4R_BUSGRP TO attunity_user The command will vary depending on the backend. Contact your SAP administrator for details.

articles.title: Scheduled DB2 iSeries task will not resume without Qlik UDTF
articles.description: Schedule is set to stop and resume tasks, but tasks will not successfully resume - task just appears to hang. Environment Qlik Replicate 2022.5 DB2 iSeries Source Resolution Issue was resolved after installing the Qlik UDTF (User Defined Table Function).
articles.text: Schedule is set to stop and resume tasks, but tasks will not successfully resume - task just appears to hang. Environment Qlik Replicate 2022.5 DB2 iSeries Source Resolution Issue was resolved after installing the Qlik UDTF (User Defined Table Function). It can increase throughput by running a filter on the iSeries to select only the transactions for the tables you want. More information on using the Qlik UDTF, including limitations, please see: Setting advanced connection properties | Qlik Replicate Help

articles.title: Selecting Tables with Underscores
articles.description: To be able to select tables with underscores you have to escape the underscore. For SQL Server source you can wrap the _ with []. Example: %[_]% would select all tables with an underscore in them.
articles.text: To be able to select tables with underscores you have to escape the underscore. For SQL Server source you can wrap the _ with []. Example: %[_]% would select all tables with an underscore in them. For sources where you need to specify the escape character you need to add the escapeCharacter internal parameter. You can then use that escape character. Example setting it to \ : %\_% would select all tables with an underscore in them. NOTE: The search button does not always work but the correct table list should be under the Full Table List. One alternative to this is to just ask the database will all its SELECT, JOIN, UNION power to generate selection to be used in the "explicit_included_tables". For example, using ORACLE SQLplus you might use: set heading off set feedback off spool explicit_included_tables.txt SELECT ' { "owner" : "' || OWNER || '", "name" : "' || TABLE_NAME || '" },' FROM ALL_TABLES WHERE OWNER = 'HR' AND TABLE_NAME NOT LIKE 'attrep%' ORDER BY OWNER, TABLE_NAME; { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "CASE_153530" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "CC_NOTE" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "COUNTRIES" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "DEPARTMENTS" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "EMPLOYEES" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "GATEWAY_REC" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "HP_QUEUE" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "HP_QUEUE2" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "JOBS" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "JOB_HISTORY" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "LOCATIONS" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "PC_ASSIGN_WORKLIST" }, { "owner" : "HR", "name" : "REGIONS" }, After that, remove the leading open squiggly bracket (curly brace) and remove closing squiggly bracket and comma. Review result, Plunk in the task JSON, Import, and the table will be selected.

articles.title: Selecting Views inside a Replicate task
articles.description: I see the following question pop up from time to time: "Why can i not select views in my Replicate task?" There can be two reason as to why you are not seeing view selection in "table selection" inside of a Replicate task: The source endpoint does not support…
articles.text: I see the following question pop up from time to time: "Why can i not select views in my Replicate task?" There can be two reason as to why you are not seeing view selection in "table selection" inside of a Replicate task: The source endpoint does not support views. Here is a list of endpoints that support view selection: Teradata (with an exception, see second point) Amazon Redshift (with an exception, see second point) PostgreSQL MySQL SAP Sybase ASE IBM DB2 for LUW IBM DB2 for z/OS Oracle Microsoft SQL Server ODBC with CDC (with an exception, see second point) ODBC Task is no selected for Full load only mode, Replication of views is supported in Full Load Only tasks, except when replicating from the following sources: Amazon Redshift Teradata ODBC with CDC

articles.title: Snowflake queries to troubleshoot queries.
articles.description: Description: The following are a few queries that are typically used to troubleshoot query patterns, warehouse usage, and credit consumption .
articles.text: Description: The following are a few queries that are typically used to troubleshoot query patterns, warehouse usage, and credit consumption . Solution: Queries for the troubleshooting: 1) Query History: USE ROLE ACCOUNTADMIN; SELECT * FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY WHERE UPPER(QUERY_TEXT) LIKE '%ACDOCA%'; Note: Make sure to filter on fields like ROWS_PRODUCED,ROWS_INSERTED,ROWS_UPDATED,ROWS_DELETED to detect query patterns Here is a complete guide on how to use the query_history view - https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/account-usage/query_history.html Note : The queries below would not be helpful right away, but are definitely worth having in the back pocket - 2) Warehouse Load History: You can look at load and consumption patterns across warehouses using the query below. Select START_TIME, END_TIME, WAREHOUSE_ID, WAREHOUSE_NAME, AVG_RUNNING, AVG_QUEUED_LOAD, AVG_QUEUED_PROVISIONING, AVG_BLOCKED from snowflake.account_usage.warehouse_load_history; Although the result for this query looks rather simple, in a visualization tool you can see overlaps in warehouse usage, combined peaks/valleys for usage. A sum of AVG_RUNNING is a good metric for combined usage. 3) Warehouse Metering History: SELECT START_TIME, END_TIME, WAREHOUSE_ID, WAREHOUSE_NAME, CREDITS_USED, CREDITS_USED_COMPUTE, CREDITS_USED_CLOUD_SERVICES from snowflake.account_usage.warehouse_metering_history; This is a similar view to the one above but is focused more on credit usage, so you could assess overall credit usage across warehouses. RVICES from snowflake.account_usage.warehouse_metering_history; This is a similar view to the one above but is focused more on credit usage, so you could assess overall credit usage across warehouses. 4) Query History SELECT USER_NAME, ROLE_NAME, WAREHOUSE_NAME, month(START_TIME) as MONTH, // you can change the granularity per your need count(QUERY_ID) from snowflake.account_usage.query_history GROUP BY 1,2,3,4; This query will give you an idea of the #queries run by users on different warehouses over a particular period (say a month, week, or year) 5) Snowflake Usage dashboard in Qlik: https://community.qlik.com/t5/Technology-Partners-Ecosystem-Documents/Qlik-amp-Snowflake-Usage-Dashb...

articles.title: SnowFlake target latency due to connectivity issues
articles.description: When SnowFlake target latency is caused by SnowFlake connectivity issues, the following configuration settings should be performed: Change the setting of SnowFlake connection string: Stop the task Go to Snowfalke endpoint target, under the advanced tab,…
articles.text: When SnowFlake target latency is caused by SnowFlake connectivity issues, the following configuration settings should be performed: Change the setting of SnowFlake connection string: Stop the task Go to Snowfalke endpoint target, under the advanced tab, additional ODBC connection string and set the following parameters: CLIENT_SESSION_KEEP_ALIVE=true;ABORT_DETACHED_QUERY=true;CLIENT_SESSION_KEEP_ALIVE_HEARTBEAT_FREQUENCY=900; Further details on these parameters can be found on SnowFlake documentation under the following link: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/index.html On the Replication Server machine, add the following registry keys: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/SOFTWARE/Snowflake/Driver/CLIENT_SESSION_KEEP_ALIVE value=true HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/SOFTWARE/Snowflake/Driver/CLIENT_SESSION_KEEP_ALIVE_HEARTBEAT_FREQUENCY value=900 HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE/SOFTWARE/Snowflake/Driver/ABORT_DETACHED_QUERY value=true For the Snowfalke user used by Replicate, perform the following settings: alter user user_name set CLIENT_SESSION_KEEP_ALIVE = TRUE; alter user user_name set ABORT_DETACHED_QUERY = TRUE; alter user user_name set CLIENT_SESSION_KEEP_ALIVE_HEARTBEAT_FREQUENCY = 900; Further details on the above setting can be found in the SnowFlake documentation under the following link: https://docs.snowflake.net/manuals/sql-reference/parameters.html#client-session-keep-alive Resume the task Environment Qlik Replicate replicating to SnowFlake target endpoint

articles.title: SQL Server cannot do an initial load and returns error that AR_PUBLICATION_0000# does not exist.
articles.description: When loading SQL server for the first time you may receive an error like: [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]W: Capture functionalities could not be set.
articles.text: When loading SQL server for the first time you may receive an error like: [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]W: Capture functionalities could not be set. RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 42000 NativeError: 20026 Message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server][SQL Server]The publication 'AR_PUBLICATION_0000#' does not exist. Line: 1 Column: -1 (sqlserver_log_utils.c:1822) Where # is some number representing a publication that Replicate has attempted to create and then reference. Environment Qlik Replicate SQL Server Source Resolution 1) Add the user that Replicate is using to interface with SQL Server to the sysadmin role 2) Let Replicate create the publication by restarting the task. This can be either a fresh start or resume as the first thing Replicate does is check for publication and articles and will create them if they do not exist. 3) Optional: remove the user from the sysadmin role Cause Replicate cannot find this publication as it failed to create it. Some SQL Server instances will have competing security rules that prevent the standard install of Replicate from creating the publication.

articles.title: SQL Server logs Length of LOB data (nnnnn) to be replicated exceeds configured maximum (xxxxx) after enabling Replication
articles.description: Environment: Qlik Replicate After having had the MS-Replication\CDC enabled on a stand-alone or AG enabled server, customer applications start getting the following errors from the database engine, when attempting any DML involving long text or LOB fields:…
articles.text: Environment: Qlik Replicate After having had the MS-Replication\CDC enabled on a stand-alone or AG enabled server, customer applications start getting the following errors from the database engine, when attempting any DML involving long text or LOB fields: “Length of LOB data to be replicated exceeds configured maximum 65536. Use the stored procedure sp_configure to increase the configured maximum value for max text repl size option, which defaults to 65536. A configured value of -1 indicates no limit, other that the limit imposed by the data type. The statement has been terminated” This error means that the length of a text , ntext , varchar(max) , nvarchar(max) , varbinary(max) , xml , or image data field participating in INSERT\UPDATE or INSERTTEXT\UPDATETEXT DML is exceeding the configured value of 65536 (a SQL server default). There is a configuration “ max text repl size (b) ” in SQL Server which can be viewed by sp_configure system procedure or querying sys.configurations system table. This parameter has an impact on systems configured with replication and\or Change Data Capture. From the above picture and the description of ‘ max text repl size (B) ’ configuration it becomes clear that the value of the parameter denotes the maximum length in bytes of a text field in replication. However, we need to understand the threshold is also applicable to other datatypes such as T ext , N text , V archar(max) , N varchar (max) , V arbinary (max) , XML , and image data types as well. SQL S erver will return this error each time the length of the data in the DML is greater than the established threshold . The DML operation gets terminated for the same reason. ge data types as well. SQL S erver will return this error each time the length of the data in the DML is greater than the established threshold . The DML operation gets terminated for the same reason. Environment: Qlik Replicate SQL Server Explanation When replication is enabled from Qlik Replicate with admin access to the DB, all the artifacts necessary for the replication will get created (articles, publications, etc…). Once this is done, additional data will start getting written into the database’s transactional log (TLOG) to allow the SQL Server log-based replication. Together with limited size data types, extended datatypes (like LOBs [Large Objects]) will need to be written to the log, which could be a costly endeavor for the database. To prevent any negative impact of long text or LOBs being written to the TLOG, SQL server by default limits the size of “replicateable” LOBs with the “Max Text Repl Size (B)” database parameter (see the image below). This can affect the applications, as any DML containing a field longer than the maximum threshold defined by “ max text replicate size ” parameter will be terminated by SQL server with a message “Length of LOB data ( affected value length ) to be replicated exceeds configured maximum ( configured length )”. As a result, any application that attempts to modify any LOB value in the database may fail with an error like the one shown below: 2022-04-06 08:46:26.267994;Information;GILM.Domain.Scheduling.TaskBase.ExecuteExportAndMaintenanceTasks: Length of LOB data (15124640) to be replicated exceeds configured maximum 65536. Use the stored procedure sp_configure to increase the configured maximum value for max text repl size option, which defaults to 65536. A configured value of -1 indicates no limit, other that the limit imposed by the data type. The statement has been terminated. red maximum value for max text repl size option, which defaults to 65536. A configured value of -1 indicates no limit, other that the limit imposed by the data type. The statement has been terminated. 2022-04-06 08:46:26.283620;Information;GILM.Domain.Scheduling.TaskBase.ExecuteExportAndMaintenanceTasks: at System.Data.SqlClient.SqlConnection.OnError(SqlException exception, Boolean breakConnection, Action`1 wrapCloseInAction) at System.Data.SqlClient.TdsParser.ThrowExceptionAndWarning(TdsParserStateObject stateObj, Boolean callerHasConnectionLock, Boolean asyncClose) at System.Data.SqlClient.TdsParser.TryRun(RunBehavior runBehavior, SqlCommand cmdHandler, SqlDataReader dataStream, BulkCopySimpleResultSet bulkCopyHandler, TdsParserStateObject stateObj, Boolean& dataReady) at System.Data.SqlClient.SqlDataReader.TryConsumeMetaData() at System.Data.SqlClient.SqlDataReader.get_MetaData() at System.Data.SqlClient.SqlCommand.FinishExecuteReader(SqlDataReader ds, RunBehavior runBehavior, String resetOptionsString, Boolean isInternal, Boolean forDescribeParameterEncryption, Boolean shouldCacheForAlwaysEncrypted) at System.Data.SqlClient.SqlCommand.RunExecuteReaderTds(CommandBehavior cmdBehavior, RunBehavior runBehavior, Boolean returnStream, Boolean async, Int32 timeout, Task& task, Boolean asyncWrite, Boolean inRetry, SqlDataReader ds, Boolean describeParameterEncryptionRequest) at System.Data.SqlClient.SqlCommand.RunExecuteReader(CommandBehavior cmdBehavior, RunBehavior runBehavior, Boolean returnStream, String method, TaskCompletionSource`1 completion, Int32 timeout, Task& task, Boolean& usedCache, Boolean asyncWrite, Boolean inRetry) at System.Data.SqlClient.SqlCommand.RunExecuteReader(CommandBehavior cmdBehavior, RunBehavior runBehavior, Boolean returnStream, String method) at System.Data.SqlClient.SqlCommand.ExecuteScalar() at Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Data.Database.DoExecuteScalar(IDbCommand command) at Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Data.Database.ExecuteScalar(DbCommand command) at GILM.Utilities.Common.DatabaseAdapter.ExecuteScalar(SQLStatement sqlStatement, String connectionStringName) in D:\TB2\56\s\GILM.Utilities.Common\Persistence\DataAccess\DatabaseAdapter.cs:line 22 Resolution To allow a database process large object datatypes while the database is enabled for replication, it will need to be configured consistently to allow longer LOBs in replication. .cs:line 22 Resolution To allow a database process large object datatypes while the database is enabled for replication, it will need to be configured consistently to allow longer LOBs in replication. A simple solution would be to set the configuration 'max text repl size (b) ' to a value of -1 allowing value s of any supported size. However, this may have some detrimental impact on replication as the size increases, we need to make sure the replication has no other side effects due to the size of the data to be replicated over the network etc. To be less generic, a following approach is recommended: Identify if there are any replication/CDC configured with the table/database Identify the LOB datatype column(s) in the affected table(s) Assess your data and conclude the maximum length of data it can reach up to as per the business requirement. Note that special handling may be required for multi-byte encodings. As an example, a photo field can be restricted with a specified size through application that can be uploaded etc. Assess the max size or length of the data in the table and confirm that the size of the data is exceeding the configured value of “max text repl size (B)” Set the required or expected size for ‘max text repl size (B)’ configuration if possible, instead of the generic maximum -1 CLI USE DBNAME; GO EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options',1 RECONFIGURE WITH OVERRIDE; GO EXEC sp_configure 'max text repl size (B)', -1 RECONFIGURE WITH OVERRIDE; GO EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options',0 RECONFIGURE WITH OVERRIDE; GO GUI Right-click on Server Level and go to Properties Open Advanced in the menu to the left Locate Max text Replication Size in the Miscellaneous section Enter your desired value.

articles.title: SQL Server Source:  Qlik Replicate encountered third-party backup files during preliminary processing
articles.description: SQL Server Source: Qlik Replicate encountered third-party backup files during preliminary processing This applies when using SQL Server as a source endpoint.
articles.text: SQL Server Source: Qlik Replicate encountered third-party backup files during preliminary processing This applies when using SQL Server as a source endpoint. WARNING: [SOURCE_CAPTURE ]W: Replicate encountered third-party backup files during preliminary processing. As the 'Use third-party backup device' option is currently disabled, these files will not be processed for changes. (sqlserver_log_queries.c:3425) This means that if the task needs to reference a backup log, we will not be able to as that file will be in the 3rd party format. Resolution You need to identify if you are using a 3rd part backup as opposed to native SQL. Virtual log backups are usually done by 3rd party SQL server backup programs, like Litespeed, Red gate etc. or by other 3rd party software like Symantec NetBackup, Commvault. Please note that Qlik Replicate by default is not reading such backup logs, and so we give the warning that such virtual backups exist. If you have such virtual backups, but they are not related to your regular transaction log backup process, and those backups don’t contain any changes that are relevant to replication, or they are done as "COPY_ONLY", Then you can ignore this warning. If you are using virtual backups as your regular backup option for SQL Server, then you will need to do both steps: Mark the "select virtual backup device types" in the SQL server source database settings in Replicate->Advanced tab Note that doing (1) will cause Replicate to try and read those virtual backup logs , but since replicate can't read 3rd party backup logs, you will need to provide to Replicate a conversion utility, in order to convert each such tlog to a native SQL server format.

articles.title: SQL Server Transaction Deadlocks
articles.description: Understanding what is a SQL Server Transaction Deadlock: When a SQL Server task fails with the following error, your transactions have encountered a Deadlock.
articles.text: Understanding what is a SQL Server Transaction Deadlock: When a SQL Server task fails with the following error, your transactions have encountered a Deadlock. RetCode: SQL_ERROR SqlState: 40001 NativeError: 1205 Message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server][SQL Server]Transaction (Process ID 966) was deadlocked on lock resources with another process and has been chosen as the deadlock victim. Rerun the transaction. “Transaction was deadlocked” error occurs when two or more sessions are waiting to get a lock on a resource which has already locked by another session in the same blocking chain. As a result, none of the sessions can be completed and SQL Server has to intervene to solve this problem. It gets rid of the deadlock by automatically choosing one of the sessions as a victim and kills it allowing the other session to continue. In such case, the client receives the following error message: Transaction (Process ID) was deadlocked on lock resources with another process and has been chosen as the deadlock victim. Rerun the transaction. and the killed session is rolled back. As a rule, the victim is the session that requires the least amount of overhead to roll back. For more information on deadlocks and how to find the related processes, view the link below. https://sqlbak.com/academy/tra nsaction-process-id-was-deadlo cked-on-lock-resources-with-an other-proc... After identified processes are no longer running on the same table and locking it, your task will be able to resume normally. Environment Qlik Replicate SQL Server The information in this article is provided as-is and to be used at own discretion.
